fields.name: FlexDDC
fields.description:
Objective:

  • Collect a high volume of diverse data across several operational design domains (ODDs) to enable Data-Driven Autonomy and the development of the Virtual Validation Platform to deliver a competitive AD/ADAS product in FY27. 

Scope:

  1. Design, build, and deploy DDC and APR vehicles for data collection and testing/validation.  
    1. DDC (Development Data Collection): No Vehicle Controller capability
    2. APR (Autonomous Public Road): Vehicle Controller capability
  2. Close the gap in data diversity and volume:
    1. Enabling a highly data-driven NaviPilot/Highway Teammate (HTM) for the BEV Step 3 (BEVS3) SOP (Start of Production)
    2. Accelerating the demonstration of Urban Teammate (UTM) capabilities targeted for 2027
  3. Conduct full autonomy stack testing on public roads
    1. Serving as ground truth for virtual validation platform
    2. Significantly enhancing the fidelity of the simulation platform used for developing and validating the autonomy stack. 

Goals: 

  • Develop ODD model: Formulate data collection and public road validation strategy, build and operationalize DDC and APR to execute against data collection and validation strategy
  • Collect diverse data
  • Validate Virtual Validation fidelity: Conduct Public Road testing and re-simulate to validate virtual validations systems ability to reproduce and identify issues
  • Scale the operations: End state is to rely heavily on MDC and ghost mode
  • Drive 250k hrs of data: 10s of millions of scenes, support 1b km of simulation per year (to train and evaluate system performance)

fields.name: Conflict Zone
fields.description:
Conflict zones are locations where the ego and ado vehicles paths merge, or cross each other

For example : In or on the approaches to an intersections, neighboring lanes and center turn lanes.

fields.name: Drieway
fields.description:
A driveway is a type of private road for local access to one or a small group of structures, and is owned and maintained by an individual or group.

Driveways rarely have traffic lights, but some that bear heavy traffic, especially those leading to commercial businesses and parks, do.

fields.name: Designated Bike Lane
fields.description: Designated bike lanes (e.g., class II bikeways) are separated by solid lane lines of different styles.  In general, cars should not enter their bike lane unless making a turning maneuver into a driveway or in the mutual conflict zone at an intersection.

fields.name: Entry Crosswallk
fields.description: The entry crosswalk (CW) is the first crosswalk that the ego vehicle crosses when traversing an intersection.

fields.name: Exit Crosswalk
fields.description: The exist crosswalk (CW) is the last crosswalk that the ego vehicle crosses when traversing an intersection.

fields.name: Footprint
fields.description: A rectangular box completely containing the vehicle, including the mirrors. The length of the box is equal to the overall vehicle length (OAL). The width of the box is equal to the overall vehicle width (OAW). The foot print is the top-down view of a BOUNDING BOX.

fields.name: Green solid light
fields.description: The green solid light indicates that the traffic can proceed in that direction of travel and there is no need to stop at an intersection

fields.name: Hard Boundary
fields.description: A hard boundary is defined as any road infrastructure that the ego vehicle cannot physically cross e.g. curb, guard rails, etc.

fields.name: Hard Brake
fields.description: Immediate slamming on brakes or System performing very strong braking TBD m/s2 i.e at the safety and jerk limits possible could be defined as Hard braking.

fields.name: Hard Handback
fields.description: A response by the ego vehicle where the vehicle automatically disengages Autonomy and hands back the control to the safety driver.

fields.name: Inside Turn
fields.description: The turning maneuver of the ego vehicle that does not include passing through any oncoming traffic lanes is an Inside Turn.

fields.name: Intersection interior
fields.description: The center portion of the traffic intersection area which does not belong to the multiple road segments that form the intersection. This is usually one example of a Keep Clear Zone.

fields.name: Keep Clear Zone (KCZ)
fields.description:
The Keep Clear Zones(KCZ) are areas that need to be left clear of any vehicles for a special purpose like the following:

  • Intersections
  • School bus stop zones
  • No parking areas (No stopping or standing anytime areas)
  • Fire truck/hydrant stop zones
  • Bike lanes 
  • Marked crosswalks
  • Bus stop 
  • Other marked "Keep Clear" areas

fields.name: Lane Borrowing
fields.description: The ego vehicle performing a lateral maneuver into an adjacent lane, occupying part or all of the adjacent lane temporarily.

fields.name: Lane Boundaries
fields.description: The right and left edges of the lane. The lane boundaries are usually marked by the white, yellow solid or dashed line lane markings, cat eyed lane dividers, other type of dividers like medians, or simply the edge of the pavement.

fields.name: Lane Change
fields.description: A lane change is a maneuver with three distinct phases: (1) activation of turn signal, (2) lateral movement across the lane boundary separating the original and target lanes, and (3) cancellation of the turn signal.

fields.name: Leading Edge
fields.description: The front-most point of the vehicle.

fields.name: Lateral Bias
fields.description: Lateral Bias refers to an unequal left/right lateral position of a vehicle within the lane - assuming the vehicle's heading is essentially parallel with respect to the center line of the lane. A left lateral bias means the vehicle is closer to the left lane boundary than to the right lane boundary. Lateral bias may be measured from any defined reference point on the vehicle (typically the center of the rear axle or the center of mass) to a lane boundary along an axis perpendicular to the longitudinal axis of the vehicle.

fields.name: Lateral Bias in Lane
fields.description: Lateral Bias in lane indicates the actual position of the ego vehicle within the current lane of travel compared to the center of the lane. Within a specified lane of travel, the ego vehicle could bias laterally more towards the left or the right edge of the lane based on the next direction of travel as needed.

fields.name: Limit Line
fields.description: A solid white line, 12 to 24 inches wide, extending across a roadway or any portion thereof to indicate the point at which traffic is required to stop. Limit lines are often found at stop signs, yield signs, traffic lights, rail road crossings, etc.

fields.name: Oncoming Traffic
fields.description: The traffic participants or vehicles usually, that are traveling in the other directions or just passing by the ego vehicle that could at some point have a common trajectory point with the ego vehicle during the travel.

fields.name: One Way street
fields.description: A one-way street is a street either facilitating only one-way traffic, or designed to direct vehicles to move in one direction. One-way streets typically result in higher traffic flow as drivers may avoid encountering oncoming traffic or turns through oncoming traffic.

fields.name: Original Lane
fields.description: The current lane of travel of the ego vehicle in which the ego vehicle is present at this instance in time.

fields.name: Pick-up/Drop-off point
fields.description:
The point within the PUDO zone, where the vehicles come to a stop for loading and unloading of persons or cargo. Pick-up/Drop-off points within the PUDO zone will usually be marked on the maps that the ego vehicles follow.

 

These points play a crucial role in ride sharing experience in the Autonomous vehicles.

fields.name: Post Encroachment Time
fields.description: The duration of time beginning when the first vehicle clears the CONFLICT ZONE and the second vehicle enters the CONFLICT ZONE. Typically PET is assigned a positive value if the left-turning vehicle is the first to traverse the conflict zone (i.e., turns in front of the through vehicle). Conversely, if the left-turning vehicle enters the conflict zone after the through vehicle exits the conflict zone, PET is assigned a negative value.  As the magnitude of PET approaches zero, the more narrowly a collision is avoided.

fields.name: Protected Turn
fields.description: A turn is considered protected when Ego has right of way over other (oncoming) traffic. Typically, a protected turn is shown by a green arrow at the traffic light. NOTE: protected turns do NOT grant right-of-way over pedestrian movements.

fields.name: PUDO zone
fields.description:
PUDO - Pick-up and Drop-Off 

 

PUDO zones are typically complex, congested areas, such as the loading zone near a hotel lobby.  In these areas, there are likely to be many of pedestrians performing a number of tasks, such as loading/unloading luggage, waiting for transport vehicles, walking to/from the hotel lobby.  The level of complexity is high and it can be difficult to predict pedestrian intent.  In addition, there may be many vehicles, including taxis and buses that may decrease visibility of pedestrians, may unpredictably start moving, and may cause pedestrians to enter/exit the roadway unexpectedly.  Finally, these zones can have ambiguous traffic flow rules with double-parked vehicles, no lane markings, no posted speed limit, and sometimes unclear directional control of traffic.  For all of these reasons, it is important to drive slowly and cautiously in these potentially congested zones.

fields.name: Red Arrow Light
fields.description: The red arrow traffic light usually indicates that the traffic in the direction of the arrow should come to a stop until there is another indication to move.

fields.name: Red solid light
fields.description: The red solid traffic lights represent an indication for all the traffic to stop before entering the intersection. It looks like in the figure below.

fields.name: Road speed limit
fields.description: The maximum speed at which the vehicles can travel on that particular road segment enforced by law in that geographical location.

fields.name: Roadway
fields.description:
ROADWAY includes portions of the highway adjacent to the traveled way, such as shoulders, slopes, ditches, channels, and related areas which are located within a road right-of-way. For SURFACE STREETS, the regions of interest may include sidewalks, driveways, crosswalks, bike lanes, medians or dividers, and other areas in close proximity to the ROADWAY.

 

[Image of roadway]

fields.name: Round About
fields.description: Placeholder. MBSE might already have a definition.   A roundabout is a type of circular intersection or junction in which road traffic is permitted to flow in one direction around a central island, and priority is typically given to traffic already in the junction

fields.name: Safety Driver
fields.description: The human driver who has the responsibility of taking over the control of the ego vehicle when the ego vehicle HARD HANDBACKs.

fields.name: Sidewalk
fields.description: A sidewalk, pavement, footpath, or footway, is a path along the side of a road. Usually constructed of concrete or asphalt, it is designed for pedestrians.

fields.name: Signalized Intersection
fields.description: The intersection where the traffic elements or participants are controlled by the traffic signal lights.

fields.name: Static Object
fields.description: Static objects are objects which never move by themselves e.g., debris, road dividers, etc.

fields.name: Stop Line
fields.description: A stop line is a type of marking used to inform drivers of the point where they are required to stop at an intersection or roundabout controlled by a stop sign or traffic signal.

fields.name: Stop Region
fields.description: A STOP REGION is the location on the road surface where the ego vehicle is legally required to stop. This may is usually behind a clearly marked limit line, but if none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection, or if none, then at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting roadway before entering it.

fields.name: Stopped Object
fields.description: Stopped objects are objects which can move suddenly e.g. stopped(parked) cars/motorbikes/bikes with a driver, pedestrians, etc.

fields.name: Surface Street
fields.description: A street that is not a freeway and has at-grade intersections with other surface streets. An ordinary city street, that is not a freeway; is at ground level, unlike elevated freeways.

fields.name: Traffic Light
fields.description: Traffic lights, also known as traffic signals, signal lights, and stop lights, and also known technically as traffic control signals, are signaling devices positioned at road intersections, pedestrian crossings and other locations to control competing flows of traffic.

fields.name: Unprotected Turn
fields.description: A turning movement where the turning vehicle must yield right-of-way to vehicles crossing the ego vehicle's intended path

fields.name: U-Turn
fields.description: A turn that can be made by the traffic participants or vehicles that resembles the letter "U" . Especially, a 180-degree turn made by a vehicle on the road

fields.name: Vulnerable Road User
fields.description: Vulnerable road user is a term applied to those most at risk in traffic, i.e. those unprotected by an outside shield. Pedestrians, pedal cyclists, and motor cyclists are accordingly considered as vulnerable since they benefit from little or no external protective devices that would absorb energy in a collision.

fields.name: Yellow solid light
fields.description: The yellow solid traffic light indicates that the traffic in that direction of travel could proceed with caution and be ready to stop at any point in time.

fields.name: Yield
fields.description: Allowing or considering other vehicles to make their maneuvers, following etiquette while sharing the same intersection or same space on the road at some point in time.A driver who stops or slows down to let another vehicle through has yielded the right of way to that vehicle.

fields.name: Yield sign
fields.description:
In road transport, a yield or give way sign indicates that merging drivers must prepare to stop if necessary to let a driver on another approach proceed. A driver who stops or slows down to let another vehicle through has yielded the right of way to that vehicle

 

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yield_sign

fields.name: Driveable Space
fields.description: The driveable space, is a portion of the road where vehicles are expected and legally allowed to occupy temporarily or permanently.

fields.name: Compatibility
fields.description: Requirements ensuring the system works well with other systems or components, including backward compatibility and interoperability.

fields.name: TSR1.1
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL transition the system from PowerOff → ControlOff when the system is powered on.

fields.name: TSR1.2
fields.description:
The ADU-PC SHALL transition the system from ControlOff → HandsOff when ACC is enabled, provided:
-No strong steer input is detected.
-A valid trajectory is available.
-Special state conditions (SplStateActive) are met.

fields.name: TSR1.3
fields.description:
The ADU-PC SHALL transition the system from HandsOffAssist → DOT Normal when:
Vehicle speed exceeds 15 km/h OR
Brake pedal is pressed.
Guard Conditions: No strong steer, and ACC is either disabled or the brake is pressed.

fields.name: TSR1.4
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL transition the system from HandsOffAssist → FadeOutToManualDrive when strong steer is detected with steering torque > 3.0 N*m.

fields.name: TSR1.5
fields.description:
The ADU-PC SHALL transition the system from HandsOffAssist → DOT Stop when:
Vehicle speed is below 5 km/h.
Brake pedal is pressed.
No strong steer input is detected.

fields.name: TSR1.7
fields.description:
The ADU-PC SHALL transition the system from DOT Normal → DOT Stop when vehicle speed drops below 5 km/h, provided:
No strong steer input is detected.
No left or right grip detected.

fields.name: TSR1.8
fields.description:
The ADU-PC SHALL transition the system from DOT Normal → FadeOutToManualDrive when:
Hands on the steering wheel detected OR
Strong steer input detected (Steering torque > 3.0 N*m).

fields.name: TSR1.9
fields.description:
The ADU-PC SHALL transition the system from DOT Deceleration → DOT Stop when:
Vehicle speed drops below 5 km/h.
No strong steer input is detected.
No left or right grip detected.

fields.name: TSR1.10
fields.description:
The ADU-PC SHALL transition the system from DOT Deceleration → FadeOutToManualDrive when:
Hands on the steering wheel detected OR
Brake/Throttle is pressed after 4+ seconds in DOT Deceleration state.
Guard conditions: LeftGrip, RightGrip, StrongSteer, OR (StayInDOTDeceleration ≥ 4 sec AND (BrakePedal OR Accelerator pressed)).

fields.name: TSR1.11
fields.description:
The ADU-PC SHALL transition the system from DOT Stop → FadeOutToManualDrive when:
Brake or accelerator is pressed

fields.name: TSR1.12
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL transition the system from FadeOutToManualDrive → ControlOff immediately upon request.

fields.name: FSR-2
fields.description: Functional safety requirement 2

fields.name: TSR2.1
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL only allow the system to transition from ControlOff to HandsOff if a valid trajectory is available.

fields.name: TSR2.2
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL only allow the system transition to autonomy state if no strong steer input is detected.

fields.name: TSR2.3
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL only allow the system to transition to autonomy state if no manual braking or acceleration inputs are detected.

fields.name: TSR2.4
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL only allow the system to transition to autonomy state if no active system faults are present in ADU-PC, SCALEXIO, actuators, or autonomy sensors. (The faults could include hardware, software and communication interface related faults).

fields.name: TSR2.5
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL only allow the system to transition to autonomy state if there is required sensor availability and perception readiness

fields.name: TSR2.6
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL only allow the system to transition to autonomy state if valid HD or EnSD map data is available.

fields.name: TSR2.7
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL display an HMI confirmation message before allowing autonomy state engagement.

fields.name: TSR2.8
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL require double confirmation (e.g., pressing ACC twice or holding the button press for 1 second) to enter autonomy state.

fields.name: TSR2.9
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL send a display message indicating the reason for engagement failure.

fields.name: TSR2.10
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL implement a safety mechanism (E-stop) to stop transmission of vehicle control command requests from the AK within 10 ms of activation of the safety mechanism

fields.name: TSR2.11
fields.description:
The ADU-PC SHALL ensure that the system be in a "Ready" state before engaging HandsOff or Autonomy state only when the following conditions are satisfied:
-SCALEXIO error notification is False AND
-ADU-PC is receiving required cyclic messages from SCALEXIO AND
-No CAN Error is reported by SCALEXIO (especially from ECB, EHV, EPS) AND
-There is a valid trajectory tube AND
-Transition Demand (TD) request is False AND
-Driver autonomy request (button press) is False AND
-Steer torque magnitude is < 4 N*m AND
-The handwheel angle is between [-40, +40] degrees AND
-No CAN error is reported by SCALEXIO (ECB failure, EHV failure, EPS failure, others?)
-The steering zero angle flag is valid AND
-No OEM intervention detected (ABS activation, VSC activation, DSC activation, others?)
-Vehicle speed < TOD limit
-Gear select switch status == DRIVE
-Brake pedal status Active
-Throttle pedal status Active

fields.name: TSR2.12
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL ensure a smooth transition of the system between ControlOff and HandsOffAssist state. (Smoothing out the control signals between the human and the system inputs if possible).

fields.name: FSR-3
fields.description: Functional Safety Requirement 3

fields.name: TSR3.7
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL immediately transition the system to manual state when the driver presses the Emergency Stop (E-Stop) button, overriding all other conditions.

fields.name: TSR3.7
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL provide HMI feedback confirming the transition from HandsOff to ControlOff. (A dashboard message (or sound alert) should indicate that the vehicle is ready to enter autonomy state)

fields.name: TSR3.6
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL ensure that disengagement does not occur abruptly at high speeds and instead follows a fade-out mechanism.

fields.name: TSR3.5
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL include an override delay (0.5 - 1 sec buffer) to prevent accidental disengagement due to minor or unintended driver inputs.

fields.name: TSR3.4
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL only transition the system from HandsOff to ControlOff state when the gear status is in Drive.

fields.name: TSR3.3
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL transition the system from HandsOff to ControlOff when throttle input is detected.

fields.name: TSR3.2
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL transition the system from HandsOff to ControlOff when the brake pedal is pressed.

fields.name: TSR3.1
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL transition the system from HandsOff to ControlOff when steering torque exceeds 3.0 N*m.

fields.name: FSR-4
fields.description: Functional Safety Requirement 4

fields.name: TSR4.12
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL log all transitions to manual state due to SCALEXIO or ADU-PC failures for diagnostics and fault analysis.

fields.name: TSR4.11
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL ensure that no active control commands are sent from autonomy once a failure-triggered transition to manual state is initiated.

fields.name: TSR4.10
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL provide an HMI alert (visual + audible warning) when transitioning to manual state due to a failure.

fields.name: TSR4.9
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL transition to manual control if a CAN bus failure persists for more than 100 ms.

fields.name: TSR4.8
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL initiate a manual takeover sequence if no valid communication is received from ADU-PC.

fields.name: TSR4.7
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL transition to manual state via the DOT state if no response is received from SCALEXIO within X ms.

fields.name: TSR4.6
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL log SCALEXIO failures and disengagement events for diagnostic purposes.

fields.name: TSR4.5
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL activate an HMI alert with a Yellow LED and an audible warning to notify the driver of a SCALEXIO failure.

fields.name: TSR4.4
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL allow disengagement using brake or throttle input if the vehicle is in DOT Stop (below 5 km/h).

fields.name: TSR4.3
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL allow disengagement using steering, brake, or throttle input if the vehicle is in DOT Deceleration (between 5-15 km/h).

fields.name: TSR4.2
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL require steering input for disengagement if the vehicle is in DOT Normal (above 15 km/h).

fields.name: TSR4.1
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL transition the system to DOT state upon detecting a SCALEXIO failure, enabling driver takeover.

fields.name: FSR-5
fields.description: Functional Safety Requirement 5

fields.name: TSR5.4
fields.description: The driver must be bale to assume full control of the vehicle when an ADU-PC failure is detected via HMI indication.

fields.name: TSR5.5
fields.description: The system SHALL log all ADU-PC failures and the corresponding transitions for diagnostic purposes.

fields.name: TSR5.1
fields.description: Upon ADU-PC failure, SCALEXIO SHALL activate an audible alert (beeping) and flash Red LED 1.

fields.name: TSR5.2
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL set all control commands (steering, throttle, and braking) to zero upon ADU-PC failure.

fields.name: TSR5.3
fields.description: The system SHALL not send any active control commands from autonomy if ADU-PC is non-functional.

fields.name: FSR-6
fields.description: Functional Safety Requirement 6

fields.name: TSR6.3
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL log all state machine failures and the corresponding manual transitions for post-event analysis.

fields.name: TSR6.2
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL implement failsafe redundancy mechanisms to prevent unintended actuation(acceleration,steering and braking) during a transition.

fields.name: TSR6.1
fields.description: If a state machine failure occurs, the ADU-PC SHALL default the system to manual state, requiring driver intervention.

fields.name: FSR-7
fields.description: Functional Safety Requirement 7

fields.name: TSR7.7
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL log all hard handback events, including trigger conditions and driver response times, for post-event analysis.

fields.name: TSR7.6
fields.description: If the vehicle is in DOT Deceleration (5-15 km/h), the ADU-PC SHALL require both steering and brake/throttle confirmation before disengagement.

fields.name: TSR7.5
fields.description: If the vehicle is in DOT Stop (below 5 km/h), the ADU-PC SHALL require brake or throttle confirmation before full manual control is enabled.

fields.name: TSR7.4
fields.description: If the vehicle is in DOT Normal (above 15 km/h), the ADU-PC SHALL require hands-on steering confirmation before allowing the driver to take full control of the vehicle.

fields.name: TSR7.3
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL activate an HMI alert (audible + visual) to notify the driver that manual control is required.

fields.name: TSR7.2
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL immediately set throttle, brake, and steering commands to zero upon a hard handback or when the gear status is not DRIVE.

fields.name: TSR7.1
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL initiate a hard handback when a system failure requires immediate driver intervention (e.g., SCALEXIO or ADU-PC failure).

fields.name: FSR-8
fields.description: Functional Safety Requirement 8

fields.name: TSR8.6
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL log all emergency braking events for diagnostic and safety analysis.

fields.name: TSR8.5
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL ensure that emergency braking activation does not conflict with driver-initiated braking inputs.

fields.name: TSR8.4
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL provide an HMI warning (visual + audible) when emergency braking is triggered due to a critical failure.

fields.name: TSR8.3
fields.description: The emergency braking system within the ADU-PC SHALL bring the vehicle to a safe stop while ensuring controlled deceleration.

fields.name: TSR8.2
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL automatically engage emergency braking if a critical failure is detected in SCALEXIO while in any DOT state.

fields.name: TSR8.1
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL automatically engage emergency braking if a critical failure is detected in ADU-PC while in any DOT state.

fields.name: FSR-9
fields.description: Functional Safety Requirement 9

fields.name: TSR9.9
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL monitor message update times and detect stale messages within X ms.

fields.name: TSR9.11
fields.description: The system SHALL establish a defined perception reaction time threshold and ensure adherence to prevent delayed responses to environmental changes.

fields.name: TSR9.10
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL ensure that end-to-end latency for processing critical safety commands does not exceed a defined threshold TBD ms.

fields.name: TSR9.8
fields.description: SCALEXIO SHALL convert CAN messages to Ethernet messages, and ADU-PC SHALL validate the timeliness and integrity of these messages.

fields.name: TSR9.7
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL detect the absence of a CAN message from other subsystems within 100 ms and flag a communication failure.

fields.name: TSR9.6
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL detect the absence of an Ethernet message from SCALEXIO within X ms and initiate a fault-handling sequence.

fields.name: TSR9.5
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL detect and reject invalid controller commands before relaying them to actuators.

fields.name: TSR9.4
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL detect and report an invalid trajectory if ADU-PC does not receive a valid control command from the trajectory planner within X ms.

fields.name: TSR9.3
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL enforce an adaptive 4-second delay before transitioning from DOT Decelerate to Manual state to ensure a controlled state transition.

fields.name: TSR9.2
fields.description: The SCALEXIO SHALL detect CAN communication failures exceeding 100 ms and transition to a safe state.

fields.name: TSR9.1
fields.description: SCALEXIO SHALL update its control frame at a rate of 4 ms to ensure real-time control feedback.

fields.name: FSR-10
fields.description: Functional Safety Requirement 10

fields.name: TSR10.4
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL log all detected stale messages for diagnostic purposes and fault analysis.

fields.name: TSR10.3
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL implement fault detection mechanisms if stale messages persist beyond the defined time window.

fields.name: TSR10.2
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL detect and discard outdated trajectory and control commands that arrive after X ms.

fields.name: TSR10.1
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL reject control commands if their latency exceeds the permissible end-to-end threshold.

fields.name: FSR-11
fields.description: Functional Safety Requirement 11

fields.name: TSR11.4
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL implement fault detection and fail-operational mechanisms if a primary sensor (camera, radar, or lidar) becomes unreliable.

fields.name: TSR11.3
fields.description: The ADU-PCSHALL ensure lane identification using an EnSD-based localization system with OMS support instead of relying solely on camera-based detection.

fields.name: TSR11.2
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL use Lidar as a ground truth reference to validate HD map-based localization.

fields.name: TSR11.1
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL perform sensor cross-validation using radar and camera fusion to improve perception reliability.

fields.name: FSR-12
fields.description: Functional Safety Requirement 12

fields.name: TSR12.4
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL log perception and localization errors to track system performance and failure rates for continuous improvements.

fields.name: TSR12.3
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL implement enhanced SD maps for lane tracking, reducing reliance on real-time vision processing alone.

fields.name: TSR12.2
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL transition from camera-only lane identification to an EnSD-based lane detection approach for improved reliability in low-visibility conditions.

fields.name: TSR12.1
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL enhance localization stability and accuracy by integrating HD maps with Lidar-based ground truth validation.

fields.name: FSR-13
fields.description: Functional Safety Requirement 13

fields.name: TSR13.4
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL provide HMI alerts (visual + audible) when transitioning to manual state due to a fail-safe event.

fields.name: TSR13.3
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL log all fail-safe activations for diagnostic and safety analysis.

fields.name: TSR13.2
fields.description: The system SHALL automatically transition to manual state if ADU-PC fails to send valid control commands within X ms.

fields.name: TSR13.1
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL automatically transition the system to manual state if SCALEXIO fails to respond within X ms.

fields.name: FSR-14
fields.description: Functional Safety Requirement 14

fields.name: TSR14.12
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL provide an audible notification to the driver if the Estop button is pressed.

fields.name: TSR14.11
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL ensure LED1 (Red On) and all other LEDs Off when transitioning from FadeOutToManualDrive → ControlOff to indicate a full disengagement along with playing Sound 2.

fields.name: TSR14.10
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL provide a warning beep and turn off LED2/LED3 when transitioning from DOT Stop → FadeOutToManualDrive to indicate manual state activation.

fields.name: TSR14.9
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL turn off LED2/LED3 when transitioning from DOT Deceleration → FadeOutToManualDrive.

fields.name: TSR14.8
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL turn off LED2/LED3 when transitioning from DOT Normal → FadeOutToManualDrive to signal an unexpected disengagement.

fields.name: TSR14.7
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL keep LED2 (Green On), LED3 (Yellow On) when transitioning from DOT Normal → DOT Stop to confirm vehicle slowing.

fields.name: TSR14.6
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL ensure no sound and no LED change during DOT Normal → DOT Deceleration but SHALL provide a progressive braking cue in future updates.

fields.name: TSR14.5
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL activate LED2 (Green On), LED3 (Yellow On) and play Sound2 when transitioning from HandsOff → DOT Stop to confirm a complete stop under autonomy.

fields.name: TSR14.4
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL turn off LED2/LED3 when transitioning from HandsOff → FadeOutToManualDrive and play Sound2 to alert the driver of autonomy disengagement.

fields.name: TSR14.3
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL set LED2 (Green On), LED3 (Yellow On) when transitioning from HandsOff → DOT Normal along with Sound 2 to confirm driver readiness to takeover control.

fields.name: TSR14.2
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL activate LED2 (Blue On) and LED3 (Yellow Flashing) along with Sound1 when transitioning from ControlOff → HandsOff to indicate engagement of autonomy state.

fields.name: TSR14.1
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL activate LED1 (Red On) when transitioning from PowerOff → ControlOff to indicate system initialization.

fields.name: FSR-15
fields.description: Functional Safety Requirement 15

fields.name: TSR15.2
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL ensure Red LEDs indicate faults or critical failures, and Green LEDs indicate autonomy engagement readiness.

fields.name: TSR15.1
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL follow a consistent color scheme for LED indicators, reversing the use of Red/Green for better fault identification.

fields.name: FSR-16
fields.description: Functional Safety Requirement 16

fields.name: TSR16.8
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL adjust the 4-second stability delay in DOT Deceleration → FadeOutToManualDrive dynamically, reducing it for emergency stops but maintaining it for smoother disengagement.

fields.name: TSR16.7
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL introduce an override delay mechanism for DOT Normal → FadeOutToManualDrive, requiring sustained steer input for X ms before disengagement.

fields.name: TSR16.6
fields.description: The system SHALL require a double-tap ACC button and visual confirmation before transitioning from ControlOff → HandsOff to prevent accidental activation.

fields.name: TSR16.5
fields.description: The system SHALL require redundant confirmation (haptic feedback on throttle) before transitioning from DOT Stop → FadeOutToManualDrive to prevent accidental disengagement.

fields.name: TSR16.4
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL use dynamic speed thresholds for DOT Normal → DOT Deceleration, adapting instead of using a fixed 15 km/h threshold.

fields.name: TSR16.3
fields.description: The system SHALL introduce a grace period (0.5 - 1 second buffer) before transitioning from HandsOff → FadeOutToManualDrive to allow smoother control.

fields.name: TSR16.2
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL require hands-on steering or explicit braking input at lower speeds before transitioning from HandsOff → DOT Stop to ensure engagement.

fields.name: TSR16.1
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL require brake press or steering input before transitioning from HandsOff → DOT Normal to confirm driver readiness.

fields.name: FSR-17
fields.description: Functional Safety Requirement 7

fields.name: TSR17.1
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL provide a system readiness HMI indicator upon transitioning from PowerOff → ControlOff to confirm boot status.

fields.name: TSR17.2
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL introduce flashing Red LEDs for critical faults and Yellow LEDs for warnings when transitioning from FadeOutToManualDrive → ControlOff.

fields.name: FSR-18
fields.description: Functional Safety Requirement 18

fields.name: TSR18.5
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL provide HMI alerts to notify the driver when a critical communication failure occurs.

fields.name: TSR18.4
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL log all detected communication errors for diagnostic analysis of safety-related failures.

fields.name: TSR18.3
fields.description:
The ADU-PC SHALL implement fail-safe response mechanisms to prevent unsafe behaviors when data corruption is detected, including:
Ignoring corrupted control signals.
Defaulting control outputs to zero to prevent unintended actuation.
Triggering a transition to manual state if communication faults persist beyond the allowable threshold.

fields.name: TSR18.2
fields.description:
The ADU-PC SHALL implement timeout detection mechanisms for all communication links, ensuring:
Loss of valid data from ADU-PC to SCALEXIO triggers an immediate fault response.
Loss of valid data from ADU-PC to ADU-ECU, Perception Sensors, or Control Actuators is detected within X ms.
SCALEXIO detects missing or delayed CAN messages from actuators within 100 ms.

fields.name: TSR18.1
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL implement Cyclic Redundancy Checks (CRCs) on all ADU-PC signals to detect data corruption.

fields.name: FSR-19
fields.description: Functional Safety Requirement 19

fields.name: TSR19.8
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL transition to ControlOff state if a higher priority control request is received from the base vehicle.

fields.name: TSR19.7
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL provide HMI alerts when a critical command fails to execute due to priority conflicts or delays.

fields.name: TSR19.6
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL log all priority escalations and conflicts for post-event diagnostics and safety validation.

fields.name: TSR19.5
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL ensure that critical safety messages are never delayed or dropped due to lower-priority data traffic.

fields.name: TSR19.4
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL detect CAN bus congestion and dynamically adjust message transmission rates to prevent latency in high-priority commands.

fields.name: TSR19.3
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL monitor and enforce priority scheduling, ensuring no lower-priority command delays the execution of higher-priority safety-critical actions.

fields.name: TSR19.2
fields.description:
The ADU-PC SHALL implement runtime priority adjustments for actuation commands, ensuring:
Braking commands always take precedence over acceleration or steering under emergency conditions.
Steering commands override throttle commands when a strong steer input (>3.0 N*m) is detected.
Emergency stop signals override all other commands, including throttle and steering inputs.

fields.name: TSR19.1
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL use CAN ID-based priority management, where lower CAN IDs represent higher priority messages to ensure safety-critical signals (e.g., braking and steering commands) are processed first.

fields.name: FSR-20
fields.description: Functional Safety Requirement 20

fields.name: TSR20.6
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL ensure all diagnostic data is stored securely and is retrievable for post-event analysis.

fields.name: TSR20.5
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL detect and report perception system failures, including sensor degradation, misalignment, and missing detections.

fields.name: TSR20.4
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL detect and log actuator faults, including braking, steering, and throttle malfunctions.

fields.name: TSR20.3
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL log trajectory failures, including invalid or missing trajectory data from ADU-PC.

fields.name: TSR20.2
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL record SCALEXIO faults, including communication failures, sensor errors, and control command losses.

fields.name: TSR20.1
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL update Tlogs every 4ms to log real-time failure conditions.

fields.name: FSR-25
fields.description: Functional Safety Requirement 25

fields.name: TSR25.1
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL send turn signal activation requests to the vehicle's body control module (BCM) in accordance with the planned trajectory in the HandsOff state of operation

fields.name: TSR25.2
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL continuously monitor the external turn signal lamps and cross-check with its requested state.

fields.name: TSR25.3
fields.description: If a discrepancy between the requested and actual turn signal status is detected, the ADU-PC SHALL trigger an HMI warning to notify the driver.

fields.name: TSR25.4
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL ensure that turn signal requests are only made when a corresponding lane change or turn maneuver is planned in the HandsOff state of operation.

fields.name: TSR25.5
fields.description: When the system is in the HandsOffAssist state, driver activation of the physical turn signal stack SHALL be ignored by the ADU-PC.

fields.name: TSR25.6
fields.description: In the event of a system failure, the ADU-PC SHALL default the turn signal control to manual driver input without unintended activation.

fields.name: FSR-21
fields.description: Functional Safety Requirement 21

fields.name: TSR21.6
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL allow external diagnostic tools to retrieve fault logs via standard OBD or proprietary interfaces.

fields.name: TSR21.5
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL maintain a fault history log, tracking failures over time for predictive maintenance and troubleshooting.

fields.name: TSR21.4
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL provide fault severity levels, categorizing issues into minor, major, and critical to prioritize handling.

fields.name: TSR21.3
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL transmit fault data over CAN and Ethernet to ensure scalability and real-time diagnostics across subsystems.

fields.name: TSR21.2
fields.description:
The ADU-PC SHALL implement LED-based failure state indications, including:
Yellow LED for warnings and recoverable faults.
Red LED for critical system failures requiring immediate driver intervention.

fields.name: TSR21.1
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL integrate HMI alerts (dashboard notifications, chimes, or voice messages) for detected faults.

fields.name: FSR-22
fields.description: Functional Safety Requirement 22

fields.name: TSR22.3
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL dynamically adjust steering constraints based on vehicle speed and road curvature.

fields.name: TSR22.2
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL implement a steering angle rate limit to prevent abrupt steering changes that could destabilize the vehicle.

fields.name: TSR22.1
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL impose a maximum steering angle limit to ensure lateral deviation does not exceed TBD meters per lane.

fields.name: FSR-23
fields.description: Functional Safety Requirement 23

fields.name: TSR23.1
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL cap maximum acceleration at TBD m/s² to prevent excessive forward thrust.

fields.name: TSR23.2
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL cap maximum deceleration at TBD m/s² to prevent harsh braking.

fields.name: TSR23.3
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL implement a smooth acceleration and braking profile to enhance passenger comfort and vehicle stability.

fields.name: TSR23.4
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL adjust acceleration and deceleration limits dynamically based on road conditions, vehicle load, and environmental factors.

fields.name: FSR-24
fields.description: Functional Safety Requirement 24

fields.name: TSR24.1
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL apply lower braking force at high speeds to prevent skidding or loss of control.

fields.name: TSR24.2
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL allow higher braking force at low speeds for rapid stopping in emergency scenarios.

fields.name: TSR24.4
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL factor in road conditions (e.g., wet, icy surfaces) when determining braking limits.

fields.name: TSR24.3
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL factor in road conditions (e.g., wet, icy surfaces) when determining braking limits.

fields.name: TSR24.5
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL log all braking limit adjustments and violations for safety analysis and refinement.

fields.name: TSR24.6
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL implement redundant longitudinal and lateral control guards.

fields.name: TSR24.7
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL prevent a non-zero acceleration control request from being sent at the same time as a non-zero deceleration control request.

fields.name: Triggers and Guard conditions for State Transitions
fields.description: Safety mechanism

fields.name: FSR-1
fields.description:
The state machine SHALL transition to a DOT state if the "Cancel" button is depressed.

 

RATIONALE:

It is desirable to mimic the disengagement mechanisms of the production system.

ALLOCATED TO:
ADU-PC (ADSM)

fields.name: FRS-2
fields.description:
The system SHALL prevent unintended engagement of autonomy state. 

 

Rationale

T.B.D

fields.name: FSR-3
fields.description:
The state machine SHALL transition from a HandsOffAssist state to FadeOutToManualDrive state if a "strong" steering torque is applied. 

 

RATIONALE:

It is desirable to mimic the disengagement mechanisms of the production system.

 

ALLOCATED TO:

ADU-PC (ADSM)

fields.name: FSR-3
fields.description:
The AK state machine SHALL transition from a HandsOffAssist state to a ControlOff if the measured steering torque >= 3.0 N*m.

 

Rationale

It is desirable to mimic the disengagement mechanisms of the production system.

fields.name: FSR-4
fields.description:
The AK state machine SHALL transition from a DOT state to a ControlOff if driver places hands on steering wheel.

 

Rationale

It is desirable to mimic the disengagement mechanisms of the production system.

fields.name: FSR-5
fields.description:
The AK state machine SHALL transition to a ControlOff state if the gear select switch is not = DRIVE.

 

Rationale

It is desirable to give the safety driver numerous mechanisms to regain manual control of the vehicle.

fields.name: FSR-6
fields.description:
The AK SHALL implement a safety mechanism to stop transmission of vehicle control command requests to the base vehicle within 10 ms of activation of the safety mechanism.

 

Rationale

It is desirable to give the safety driver numerous mechanisms to regain manual control of the vehicle.

fields.name: FSR-7
fields.description:
The AK SHALL send a valid acceleration request when in the HandsOffAssist state.

 

Rationale

Only autonomy control request that meet feasibility conditions should be passed to the base vehicle.

fields.name: FSR-8
fields.description:
The AK SHALL send a valid steering angle request when in the HandsOffAssist state.

 

Rationale

Only autonomy control request that meet feasibility conditions should be passed to the base vehicle.

fields.name: FSR-10
fields.description:
The AK SHALL limit the magnitude of longitudinal acceleration/deceleration control request.

 

Rationale

Control requests sent to the base vehicle must remain within a safe performance region.

fields.name: FSR-9
fields.description:
The AK SHALL NOT send an invalid lateral or longitudinal control requests to the base vehicle.

 

Rationale

Commands that are invalid for any reason should not be carried out by the base vehicle.

fields.name: FSR-11
fields.description:
The AK state machine SHALL prevent a non-zero acceleration control request from being sent at the same time as a non-zero deceleration control request.

 

Rationale

There is no conceivable scenario where this behavior would be desirable for the AK and thus it should be avoided.

fields.name: FSR-12
fields.description:
The AK state machine SHALL transition to ControlOff state if a control request is made by the VSC-ECU.

 

Rationale

The AK should not conflict with these types of interventions that are designed to maintain dynamic stability.

fields.name: FSR-13
fields.description:
The AK SHALL require the ACC button to be continuously depressed for >= 1.0 seconds before transiitioning from the "ControlOFF" state to the "HandsOffAssist" state.

 

Rationale

This is to guard against an accidental button press from engaging autonomy without the drivers knowledge.

fields.name: FSR-14
fields.description:
The AK SHALL satisfy readiness conditions before transitioning from ControlOff to HandsOffAssist state.

 

Rationale

Before engaging autonomy, it is important to verify that the AK is ready to take over control.

fields.name: FSR-15
fields.description:
While in the any state other than (PowerOff OR HandsOffAssist), the AK SHALL send "default" control requests (i.e., zero steering angle and zero acceleration). 

 

Rationale

fields.name: FSR-16
fields.description:
While not in the PowerOff state, the AK SHALL send "default" control requests to the base vehicle if the gear select switch is not = DRIVE.

 

Rationale

The AK should only be able to make control requests to the base vehicle if the vehicle is in DRIVE as REVERSE is not yet supported.

fields.name: FSR-17
fields.description:
The AK SHALL communicate its operational state to the human driver (i.e., PowerOff, ControlOff, DOT[x], HandsOffAssist, FadeOutToManualDrive).

 

Rationale

It is important to inform the driver of what level of autonomous control is provided/possible and when the level of control changes.

fields.name: FSR-19
fields.description:
The AK SHALL provide an audible notification to the driver if requested by the SCALEXIO.

 

Rationale

It is important to inform the driver if the SCALEXIO detects an error condition.

fields.name: FSR-18
fields.description: The system SHALL ensure reliable and fault-tolerant communication between all safety-critical components.

fields.name: FSR-20
fields.description:
When AK is in the HandsOffAssist state, the state of the external turn signal lamps SHALL be consistent with the turn signal status request from the AK.

 

Rationale

In order to avoid confusing the driver or external traffic participants, the external turn signal status should be consistent with the request from the AK.

fields.name: FSR-21
fields.description:
When not in the HandsOffAssist state, the state of the external turn signal lamps SHALL be consistent with the state of the physical turn signal switch.

 

Rationale

When not in autonomy, the human driver should be responsible for controlling external turn signal behavior.

fields.name: Safety limits imposed on vehicle controls
FSR-22
fields.description: The system SHALL enforce safety limits on vehicle control outputs to prevent unintended or unsafe maneuvers.

fields.name: FSR-23
fields.description: The system SHALL enforce acceleration and deceleration constraints to ensure controlled vehicle dynamics.

fields.name: FSR-24
fields.description: The system SHALL implement adaptive braking limits based on vehicle speed and driving scenarios.

fields.name: Turn Signal Activation from Autonomy Kit
FSR-25
fields.description: The state of the external turn signal lamps SHALL be consistent with the system turn signal status requests.

fields.name: Human-In-The-Loop - Block Diagram
fields.description:
Background :

 

  • Version1.1 : Human in the loop initially was designed to follow the below sequence of steps :
  1. HITL Request
  2. Technician communicates the Request to Safety Driver
  3. Safety Driver checks environment
  4. Safety Driver approves verbally and communicates to the Technician
  5. Technician approves the HITL Request through the key combination of ctrl+shift+U
  6. System initiates HITL task

The corresponding version 1.1 of the HITL block diagram can be found in the following link : HITL Block Diagram V1.1

 

  • Version 1.2:  Currently Technician approval has been changed to Safety Driver approval as it reduces the amount of communication between the Technician and the Safety Driver to avoid any delays and miscommunication as well. Also, the key press combination of ctrl+shift+U for HITL approval has been changed to pressing ACC Button for P4 vehicles and Indicator stalk for P5 vehicles. So the current sequence of steps have been updated as follows:
  1. HITL Request
  2. Technician communicates the Request to Safety Driver
  3. Safety Driver checks environment
  4. Safety Driver approves the HITL Request through ACC button(P3/P4) or indicator stalk (P5)
  5. System initiates HITL task

The corresponding version 1.2 of the HITL block diagram can be found in the following link : HITL Block Diagram V1.2

fields.name: SG-1 Safety Driver Intervention
fields.description:
The AK shall allow the safety driver to take over control of the lateral and/or longitudinal motion of the base vehicle on safety driver's demand in a timely manner 

 

Safe State: 
ControlOff state
fields.rationale$137: If there is a loss of or an unintended lateral/longitudinal control output (Loss of Braking, Loss of Steering, Undemanded Braking, Undemanded Steering or Undemanded Acceleration), it is assumed that a trained safety driver is capable of mitigating these incorrect outputs and regain manual control of the lateral and/or longitudinal motion of the vehicle.

fields.name: SG-2 Safe Performance Area
fields.description:
The AK shall prevent lateral or longitudinal control outputs to the base vehicle if these outputs are outside the safe performance area.

 

Safe State:

Control requests outside of the safe performance limits are saturated (i.e., capped at the max allowable value) by the AK.
fields.rationale$137: Safe performance area is considered to be a set of steering rate, steering angle, acceleration, and braking ranges within which the trained safety driver have enough time to take over the controls and perform necessary mitigation actions if a risk of a collision appears.

fields.name: SG-3 Unintended Engagement Prevention
fields.description:
The AK shall prevent an unintended engagement of the AK.

 

Safe State:

If any unintended engagement occurs, the driver is made aware of the change in state via visual and/or audio cues.
fields.rationale$137: If AK provides longitudinal and/or lateral control commands when not intended by the safety driver, the safety driver may not have sufficient time to intervene before a potentially hazardous event occurs.

fields.name: SG-4 Safety Driver Awareness
fields.description: The AK shall communicate its state to the safety driver in a timely manner.
fields.rationale$137: To increase safety driver's awareness of the ADSM state, a continuous state and mode communication is required

fields.name: SG-5 External Turn Signal State
fields.description: The state of the external turn signals lamps shall be consistent with the AK turn signal status request
fields.rationale$137: To avoid confusing the external participants as well as the safety driver.

fields.name: Assumption of driving lane position
fields.description: The requirements in this project are described based on USA traffic rules. In particular, position of driving lane supposes to be in right side of roads. So when you think about Japanese roads, you have to translate the descriptions by reversing "Left" and "Right."

fields.name: FSR-1
fields.description: When all of the trigger conditions are satsified, the ADSM SHALL transition from HandsOffAssist state to DOTNormal state.

fields.name: FSR-2
fields.description: When all of the trigger conditions are satsified, the ADSM SHALL transition from HandsOffAssist state to DOTStop state.

fields.name: FSR-3
fields.description: When a strong steering torque is applied, the ADSM SHALL transition from a HandsOffAssist state to a FadeOutToManualDrive state.

fields.name: FSR-4
fields.description: When the gear select switch is moved out of DRIVE AND the ADSM is in the HandsOffAssist state, the ADSM SHALL transition from a HandsOffAssist state to a FadeOutToManualDrive state.

fields.name: FSR-5
fields.description: The AK state machine SHALL implement a safety mechanism to stop transmission of vehicle control command requests from the AK within 10 ms of activation of the safety mechanism by the driver.

fields.name: FSR-6
fields.description: The AK SHALL limit the magnitude of the longitudinal acceleration/deceleration control request sent to the base vehicle.

fields.name: FSR-7
fields.description: The AK SHALL limit the magnitude of the steering angle control request sent to the base vehicle.

fields.name: FSR-8
fields.description: The AK SHALL prevent invalid control request from being sent to the base vehicle.

fields.name: FSR-9
fields.description: The AK SHALL respect control interventions from the VSC-ECU or Dynamics Domain Controller.

fields.name: FSR-10
fields.description: The AK SHALL prevent unintended engagement of the state machine.

fields.name: FSR-11
fields.description: While the ADSM is NOT in (HandsOffAssist OR PowerOff) state, the AK SHALL prevent non-zero control request from being sent to the base vehicle.

fields.name: FSR-12
fields.description: When entering or exiting the HandsOffAssist state, the autonomy indicator SHALL provide an audible notification to the safety driver.

fields.name: FSR-13
fields.description: When AK is in the HandsOffAssist state, the state of the external turn signal lamps SHALL be consistent with the turn signal status request from the AK.

fields.name: FSR-15
fields.description: The ADU-PC SHALL detect late messages from the SCALEXIO.

fields.name: FSR-16

fields.name: FSR-17

fields.name: FSR-18
fields.description: The system SHALL automatically transition to manual state if ADU-PC fails to send valid control commands within X ms.

fields.name: FSR-19

fields.name: FSR-20
fields.description: The autonomy indicator SHALL detect loss of communication with the SCALEXIO

fields.name: FSR-21

fields.name: TSR2-1
fields.description:
When,
steering torque < 3.0 N*m AND
vehicle speed < 5.0 km/h AND
(brake pedal is pressed OR Cancel button is pressed OR control request is invalid)
, if the ADSM is in a HandsOffAssist state, then the ADSM SHALL transition to a DOTStop state.

fields.name: TSR3-1
fields.description: When the steering torque >= 3.0 N*m, if the ADSM is in a HandsOffAssist state, then the ADSM SHALL transition to a FadeOutToManualDrive state.

fields.name: TSR4-1
fields.description:
When,
gear_select_switch != Drive,
if the ADSM is in a HandsOffAssist state, then the ADSM SHALL transition to a FadeOutToManualDrive state.

fields.name: TSR5-1
fields.description: The Estop button SHALL disconnect power to the SCALEXIO and GL2400 CAN Gateways until the Estop button is reset.

fields.name: TSR5-2
fields.description: The Estop button SHALL be located within easy reach of the safety driver

fields.name: TSR5-3
fields.description: The Estop button SHALL be red in color

fields.name: TSR5-4
fields.description: The Estop button SHALL be a normally closed switch

fields.name: TSR5-5
fields.description: The Estop button SHALL be a push to activate twist to reset design

fields.name: TSR6-1
fields.description: SLIDE 16  contains maximum longitudinal acceleration/deceleration limits as a function of vehicle speed.

fields.name: TSR6-2
fields.description: SLIDE 17 contains maximum steering angle limit as a function of vehicle speed.

fields.name: TSR8-1
fields.description: If a control request is marked as "invalid", the SCALEXIO SHALL send a "default" control request in its place to the base vehicle. (Default request = zero accel, zero steering angle)

fields.name: TSR9-1
fields.description: When (CAN signal 1 == X OR CAN signal 2 == y OR ...), the AK state machine SHALL send default control requests (steering angle = 0, acceleration = 0), if the ADSM is in the HandsOffAssist state.

fields.name: TSR10-1
fields.description:
While only in the "ControlOff" state AND the "readiness conditions are satisfied", when the "ACC" button is continuously pressed for >= 1.0 seconds, then the ADSM SHALL transition to the "HandsOffAssist" state.
NOTE 1: A button press SHALL require require the detection of both a rising an falling signal edge 
NOTE 2: Readiness conditions are defined in the lines below

1. All topics monitored by the validity watcher must be valid
  - turn_indicator_message
  - controller_task
  - vehicle_pose
  - camera_{xx}_metadata
  - camera_{xx}_metadata_adas_ecu
2. control tape from controller is valid [confirm latency and freshness]
3. The following CAN messages were received within 3X their defined cycle time
     - EHV2G32 (cycle time = 32 ms)
     - EPS1S11 (cycle time = 10 ms)
     - MET1S43 (cycle time = 1000 ms)
     - MET1S44 (cycle time = 1000 ms)
     - VSC1G13 (cycle time = 20 ms)
4. Must have received a CAN message from the SCALEXIO in the last 100 ms
5. GPUs are below their critical temperature
6. camera plugin in  x_view is NOT allowed to be active
7. x_view must be publishing a "heartbeat" message at least once every 500 ms
8. steer torque < 3.0 N*m
9. SplState is active (emulated engage procedure was performed, this satisfies NOTE 1)
10. Gear select switch status == DRIVE
11. No CAN Error is reported by SCALEXIO (especially from ECB, EHV, EPS)

fields.name: TSR11-1
fields.description: While the ADSM is NOT in (HandsOffAssist OR PowerOff) state, the AK SHALL send "default" control commands (steering angle = 0, acceleration = 0) to the base vehicle.

fields.name: TSR12-1
fields.description: When entering the HandsOffAssist state, the autonomy indicator SHALL provide an audible "engage" notification to the human driver.

fields.name: TSR12-2
fields.description: When the ADSM transitions from the HandsOffAssist state to either the (DOTNormal OR DOTStop) state, the autonomy indicator SHALL provide an audible "disengage" notification to the human driver.

fields.name: TSR12-3
fields.description: When the ADSM transitions from the HandsOffAssist state to the FadeOutToManualDrive state, the autonomy indicator SHALL provide an audible "disengage" notification to the human driver.

fields.name: TSR20-1
fields.description: If the autonomy indicator receives a late message from the SCALEXIO, then the autonomy indicator SHALL provide an error notification to the driver. (LED 1 to 3 = OFF, LED 4 = Red, buzzer = ON)

fields.name: TSR20-2
fields.description: If the SCALEXIO receives a late message from the autonomy indicator, then the SCALEXIO SHALL notify the ADU-PC of the failure in the autonomy indicator.

fields.name: TSR20-3
fields.description: When in the HandsOffAssist state, If the ADU-PC receives notification of a failure in the autonomy indicator, then the ADSM SHALL exit HandsOffAssist state.

fields.name: TSR13-1
fields.description: When the ADSM is in the HandsOffAssist state, the Internal Product Driver SHALL send the turn signal request status from the Planner to the base vehicle.

fields.name: TSR13-2
fields.description: When the ADSM is in the HandsOffAssist state, the Internal Product Driver SHALL block the turn signal status message originating from the physical turn signal switch from activating the external turn signal lamps.

fields.name: TSR15-1
fields.description: When the ADSM is in the HandsOffAssist state, if the Internal Product Driver fails to receive new CAN data from the SCALEXIO within 100 milliseconds, the ADSM SHALL exit HandsOffAssist.

fields.name: TSR16-1
fields.description:
If the autonomy indicator fails to receive CAN message SST001 from the SCALEXIO, the autonomy indicaor SHALL: 
(1) display the following LED pattern [1 = OFF, 2 = OFF, 3 = OFF, 4 = RED] AND
(2) sound the buzzer for 2.0 seconds

fields.name: TSR17-1
fields.description: When the ADSM is in the HandsOffAssist state, if the Internal Product Driver fails to send a valid trajectory tube to the SCALEXIO, the ADSM SHALL exit HandsOffAssist.

fields.name: TSR18-1
fields.description: When the ADSM is in the HandsOffAssist state, if the Internal Product Driver receives message from the SCALEXIO containing a CRC error, the ADSM SHALL exit HandsOffAssist.

fields.name: TSR19-1
fields.description: If the SCALEXIO receives a message from the ADU-PC that is (late OR invalid), THEN SCALEXIO SHALL send error notification to the autonomy indicator.

fields.name: TSR7-1
fields.description: SLIDE 17 contains maximum steering angle limit as a function of vehicle speed.

fields.description:
Each system requirement should include an acceptance test and definition of what constitutes success. In this project the definition of "acceptance test" is as follows:

An acceptance is the minimum required evidence to begin testing of a feature from a closed-course environment to a public road.
