fields.name: Traffic Flow LC Customization Toggle – End-to-End Behavior
fields.description:
Verify that the Traffic Flow LC Custom State for lane change proposals based on traffic flow behaves as a toggle stored in non-volatile memory:

  • The state changes only when the customization switch transitions from 0: SW Not Pressed to 1: SW Pressing.
  • On each such rising edge, the state flips Off → On or On → Off depending on the previous non-volatile state.
  • In all other switch patterns, the state is retained.
  • The WRITE (Ms) and IOLayer outputs are always consistent with each other and with the intended state.
fields.preconditions$599:
System is powered and operating normally; no diagnostic/fault conditions active.
At test start (Cycle 0):
Custom SW for Lane Change Proposal Based on Traffic Situation (IOLayer) previous value = 0: SW Not Pressed.
Non-Volatile Traffic Flow LC Custom State (READ) (Ms) = CustomStateToggle::Off.
The implementation detects a rising edge when the Custom SW value changes from 0 to 1 between consecutive cycles.
fields.postconditions$599:
Over the full sequence of steps:
The Traffic Flow LC Custom State has toggled Off → On → Off in response to two distinct 0 → 1 transitions of the switch.
In all cycles where the switch transition is 0→0, 1→1, or 1→0, the Traffic Flow LC Custom State has remained unchanged.
In each cycle, Non-Volatile Traffic Flow LC Custom State (WRITE) (Ms) and
Non-Volatile Traffic Flow LC Custom State (IOLayer) have had the same value and matched the intended state according to the requirement.

testCaseSteps.action:
Set previous values for Cycle 1:
SW(prev) = 0: SW Not Pressed
Custom State (READ) = CustomStateToggle::Off
In Cycle 1, set SW(curr) = 0: SW Not Pressed (no press; transition 0→0).
Execute the customization state logic.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult:
Non-Volatile Traffic Flow LC Custom State (WRITE) (Ms) = CustomStateToggle::Off
Non-Volatile Traffic Flow LC Custom State (IOLayer) = CustomStateToggle::Off
testCaseSteps.notes: Confirms that without a 0→1 transition, the previous state is retained.

testCaseSteps.action:
Use as previous values for Cycle 2:
SW(prev) = 0: SW Not Pressed (from Cycle 1)
Custom State (READ) = CustomStateToggle::Off
In Cycle 2, set SW(curr) = 1: SW Pressing (transition 0→1).
Execute the customization state logic.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult:
Non-Volatile Traffic Flow LC Custom State (WRITE) (Ms) = CustomStateToggle::On
Non-Volatile Traffic Flow LC Custom State (IOLayer) = CustomStateToggle::On
testCaseSteps.notes: Verifies the rule: 0→1 with previous state Off → set current state to On.

testCaseSteps.action:
Use as previous values for Cycle 3:
SW(prev) = 1: SW Pressing
Custom State (READ) = CustomStateToggle::On (from Cycle 2)
In Cycle 3, set SW(curr) = 1: SW Pressing (transition 1→1, still pressed).
Execute the customization state logic.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult:
Non-Volatile Traffic Flow LC Custom State (WRITE) (Ms) = CustomStateToggle::On
Non-Volatile Traffic Flow LC Custom State (IOLayer) = CustomStateToggle::On
testCaseSteps.notes: Confirms that maintaining the switch in the pressed state does not cause repeated toggles.

testCaseSteps.action:
Use as previous values for Cycle 4:
SW(prev) = 1: SW Pressing
Custom State (READ) = CustomStateToggle::On
In Cycle 4, set SW(curr) = 0: SW Not Pressed (transition 1→0, release).
Execute the customization state logic.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult:
Non-Volatile Traffic Flow LC Custom State (WRITE) (Ms) = CustomStateToggle::On
Non-Volatile Traffic Flow LC Custom State (IOLayer) = CustomStateToggle::On
testCaseSteps.notes: Verifies that the falling edge does not change the customization state.

testCaseSteps.action:
Use as previous values for Cycle 5:
SW(prev) = 0: SW Not Pressed (from Cycle 4)
Custom State (READ) = CustomStateToggle::On
In Cycle 5, set SW(curr) = 1: SW Pressing (transition 0→1).
Execute the customization state logic.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult:
Non-Volatile Traffic Flow LC Custom State (WRITE) (Ms) = CustomStateToggle::Off
Non-Volatile Traffic Flow LC Custom State (IOLayer) = CustomStateToggle::Off
testCaseSteps.notes: Verifies the rule: 0→1 with previous state On → set current state to Off.

testCaseSteps.action:
Use as previous values for Cycle 6:
SW(prev) = 1: SW Pressing
Custom State (READ) = CustomStateToggle::Off (from Cycle 5)
In Cycle 6, set SW(curr) = 1: SW Pressing (transition 1→1).
Execute the customization state logic.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult:
Non-Volatile Traffic Flow LC Custom State (WRITE) (Ms) = CustomStateToggle::Off
Non-Volatile Traffic Flow LC Custom State (IOLayer) = CustomStateToggle::Off
testCaseSteps.notes: Confirms again that a held press does not change the state once toggled.

testCaseSteps.action:
Use as previous values for Cycle 7:
SW(prev) = 1: SW Pressing
Custom State (READ) = CustomStateToggle::Off
In Cycle 7, set SW(curr) = 0: SW Not Pressed (transition 1→0).
Execute the customization state logic.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult:
Non-Volatile Traffic Flow LC Custom State (WRITE) (Ms) = CustomStateToggle::Off
Non-Volatile Traffic Flow LC Custom State (IOLayer) = CustomStateToggle::Off
testCaseSteps.notes: Confirms that after the second toggle, the state remains Off across the release, finishing the Off → On → Off sequence.

fields.name: Traffic Flow LC Customization Existence Flag – Constant “Exist” Output
fields.description:
Verify that the Behavior Context outputs the Non-Volatile Traffic Flow LC Custom Exist (WRITE) (Ms) signal as

  • CustomExist::Exist at all times, so that downstream components (e.g., HMI) can always treat the traffic-flow-based lane change customization feature as present and display the corresponding customization items.
fields.preconditions$599:
- The system is powered on and operating in a normal, fault-free condition.
- The software version under test includes implementation of SWRD-PnP-LCA-LP_DynamicLc_910_SP_1.
- Any required initialization for Behavior Context and related non-volatile interfaces has completed successfully.
- No diagnostic or configuration mechanism disables the traffic-flow-based lane change customization feature (i.e., the feature is considered supported for this ECU/software variant).
fields.postconditions$599:
- For all evaluated execution cycles during this test, the output Non-Volatile Traffic Flow LC Custom Exist (WRITE) (Ms) has the value CustomExist::Exist.
- The signal Non-Volatile Traffic Flow LC Custom Exist (WRITE) (Ms) never takes any value other than CustomExist::Exist during the test (e.g., it never becomes “None”/“Not Exist”).
- The constant CustomExist::Exist output can be used by downstream components to always treat this customization feature as available, enabling the display of the corresponding customization items.

testCaseSteps.action: Power on the system and allow it to complete all standard initialization for Behavior Context and any related non-volatile memory handling. Once initialization is complete, read the value of Non-Volatile Traffic Flow LC Custom Exist (WRITE) (Ms) during the first stable execution cycle.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Immediately after initialization, the value of Non-Volatile Traffic Flow LC Custom Exist (WRITE) (Ms) is CustomExist::Exist. No intermediate or default “non-exist” value is observed once the system has reached normal operation.
testCaseSteps.notes: Verifies that the requirement is satisfied from the beginning of normal runtime and that the existence flag for the Traffic Flow LC customization feature is asserted as “Exist” as soon as the system is ready.

testCaseSteps.action: Continue running the system for several consecutive execution cycles under normal operation without introducing any configuration changes or faults. During these cycles, repeatedly observe or log the value of Non-Volatile Traffic Flow LC Custom Exist (WRITE) (Ms).
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: In every observed execution cycle, Non-Volatile Traffic Flow LC Custom Exist (WRITE) (Ms) remains CustomExist::Exist. No transitions to any other value occur while the system operates normally.
testCaseSteps.notes: Confirms that the existence flag is implemented as a constant “Exist” output over time, not just a one-shot initialization value. This demonstrates that there is no internal state or condition that can cause the flag to change away from “Exist” during normal operation.

testCaseSteps.action: If available in the test environment, vary other unrelated system conditions (for example, simulate different driving scenes, lane change states, or user customization On/Off states for other features) while continuing to monitor Non-Volatile Traffic Flow LC Custom Exist (WRITE) (Ms). Do not inject any faults or explicitly disable the traffic-flow-based customization feature.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Regardless of changes in other system conditions (e.g., lane change state, other customization settings, or scenario changes), Non-Volatile Traffic Flow LC Custom Exist (WRITE) (Ms) consistently remains CustomExist::Exist. No correlation is observed between other behaviors and this existence flag.
testCaseSteps.notes: Demonstrates that the existence flag is independent of runtime driving scenarios and other customization states, and that it reflects only the static presence of the traffic-flow-based LC customization feature for this variant.

testCaseSteps.action: If the implementation provides a diagnostic or configuration interface that can be inspected (but not modified in this test), verify that no diagnostic trouble codes or configuration parameters indicate that the traffic-flow-based LC customization feature is unsupported or disabled, while still monitoring Non-Volatile Traffic Flow LC Custom Exist (WRITE) (Ms).
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Diagnostic/status information indicates that the feature remains supported/enabled, and Non-Volatile Traffic Flow LC Custom Exist (WRITE) (Ms) continues to output CustomExist::Exist. There is no discrepancy between configuration/diagnostic status and the existence flag output.
testCaseSteps.notes: Adds confidence that the constant “Exist” output is consistent with any available configuration or diagnostic view of the feature’s presence for this ECU/software variant.

fields.name: Navigation Map-Link Lane Change – LC Proposal Section for Destination Reachability
fields.description: Verify that, based on the Long Spatial Information (MapService) for a route where at least one lane change is necessary to reach the destination, the software sets up the LC Proposal Section (Internal) such that it represents the lane-change-related section of the route that is necessary for reaching that destination.
fields.preconditions$599:
- The system is powered on and operating in a normal, fault-free condition.
The destination is set in the navigation system, and a valid route from the current vehicle position to the destination has been calculated.
- The Long Spatial Information (MapService) input provides route and lane-level data for a road segment ahead of the vehicle that includes at least one location where remaining in the current lane would prevent the vehicle from reaching the destination (e.g., an upcoming split where only one branch continues toward the destination, requiring a lane change into the correct branch).
- The test designer has identified, within the Long Spatial Information, a continuous spatial section (or set of links/segments) along the route that corresponds to the lane change necessary for reaching the destination (this is the “expected LC proposal section” for this test).
- All other inputs required to process navigation-based lane change behavior are in nominal and consistent states (e.g., no map errors, no route recalculation in progress).
fields.postconditions$599:
- For the evaluated scenario, the output LC Proposal Section (Internal) is set such that:
     - It is non-empty / validly defined (i.e., the system has established an LC proposal section).
     - It corresponds to the portion of the route identified in the Long Spatial Information as requiring a lane change to reach the destination (the expected LC proposal section defined in the precondition).
     - The boundaries and identification of the LC Proposal Section (Internal) are consistent with the lane-change-related portion of the Long Spatial Information (e.g., same sequence of links/segments, or equivalent spatial start/end along the route).
- No LC Proposal Section (Internal) is created outside of the route segment that is relevant to reaching the current destination (i.e., the output does not include unrelated or incorrect sections).

testCaseSteps.action: Configure the navigation system with a specific test route from the current vehicle position to a chosen destination such that, according to the map data, there is at least one upcoming road split or junction where staying in the current lane would lead away from the destination, and changing to another lane is necessary to continue toward the destination. Ensure that the Long Spatial Information (MapService) provided to the software contains lane-level route information for this area, including the portion of the route where the lane change is required. Identify and document, from the map data, the spatial range (e.g., link IDs, start/end distances, or equivalent representation) that constitutes the expected LC proposal section necessary for reaching the destination.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: The test route is successfully configured, and the Long Spatial Information (MapService) input clearly represents a route segment where a lane change is required to reach the destination, including a definable expected LC proposal section (e.g., from a certain distance before the junction to a certain distance after, or a set of contiguous links). The expected LC proposal section is unambiguously documented for later comparison with the system output.
testCaseSteps.notes: This step prepares a controlled scenario that matches the requirement intent: an LC is necessary to reach the destination, and the Long Spatial Information includes enough detail to define the required LC proposal section.

testCaseSteps.action: Start or continue system execution with the above route active and the vehicle (or ego position in simulation) located at a point upstream of the identified LC proposal section, such that the Long Spatial Information already covers the entire section where the lane change will be needed. Allow the perception and planning navigation logic to process the Long Spatial Information and reach a steady state for this route.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: After the system has processed the route and Long Spatial Information, the software internally determines that, to reach the destination, a lane change is necessary within the previously identified section of the route. The logic responsible for setting the LC Proposal Section (Internal) has sufficient map and route context to perform this determination.
testCaseSteps.notes: This step ensures that the system has all required upstream information from Long Spatial Information (MapService) and is in a state where it can decide which section of the route should be used as the LC proposal section for destination reachability.

testCaseSteps.action: Read or log the value of LC Proposal Section (Internal) once the system has reached a stable state for the configured route and ego position. Interpret the LC Proposal Section (Internal) according to its defined signal structure (e.g., start and end positions along the route, link IDs, or other spatial representation).
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: The LC Proposal Section (Internal) is set and represents a specific section along the route. Its spatial representation (e.g., start point, end point, and/or sequence of links) can be compared to the expected LC proposal section identified from the Long Spatial Information. The signal is valid (not unset, not an error/default value) and clearly indicates an LC proposal section.
testCaseSteps.notes: This step directly observes the output required by the specification. The key is that LC Proposal Section (Internal) is present and interpretable for comparison.

testCaseSteps.action: Compare the observed LC Proposal Section (Internal) with the expected LC proposal section documented from the Long Spatial Information in the precondition. Check that the spatial range (e.g., link IDs and order, or start/end distances) matches the lane-change-related section needed to reach the destination and that no unrelated route segments are included.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: The spatial extent and identification of LC Proposal Section (Internal) match the expected LC proposal section derived from the Long Spatial Information. Specifically, the LC Proposal Section (Internal) covers the portion of the route where the lane change is necessary to reach the destination and does not extend into route portions that are unrelated to this lane change necessity. This confirms that the system “sets up the LC proposal section necessary for reaching the destination” as described in the requirement.
testCaseSteps.notes: This step is the core verification of the requirement. It demonstrates that, given Long Spatial Information with a known lane-change-needed region, the system outputs an LC Proposal Section (Internal) that corresponds to that region and is specifically tied to destination reachability.

testCaseSteps.action: Optionally repeat the above procedure with one or more additional test routes where the location and structure of the lane-change-needed section differ (e.g., different junction geometry, multiple consecutive lane changes required), while keeping the feature enabled and the system in a nominal state. For each route, identify the expected LC proposal section from the Long Spatial Information and compare it with the observed LC Proposal Section (Internal).
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: For each additional test route, the LC Proposal Section (Internal) correctly reflects the lane-change-related section that is necessary for reaching the destination as defined by the Long Spatial Information. Across all routes, no case is observed where LC Proposal Section (Internal) is missing when an LC is necessary for the destination, or where it indicates a section that is not needed for reaching the destination.
testCaseSteps.notes: This step increases coverage and confidence that the behavior is not limited to a single route configuration, and that the system consistently sets the LC Proposal Section (Internal) based on the Long Spatial Information whenever a lane change is necessary to reach the destination.

fields.name: Navigation Map-Link Lane Change – LC Proposal Section for Lane Reduction
fields.description: Verify that, based on the Long Spatial Information (MapService) input, the software sets an LC Proposal Section (Internal) for road segments where a lane reduction occurs, so that an LC proposal section (Auto section) is established in relation to lane reduction points along the route.
fields.preconditions$599:
- The system is powered on and operating in a normal, fault-free condition.
- A valid navigation route from the current vehicle position to a destination has been calculated.
- The Long Spatial Information (MapService) input provides lane-level route data for a road segment ahead of the vehicle that includes at least one lane reduction (for example, a transition from three lanes to two lanes in the direction of travel, where one lane ends).
- The test designer has identified, from the Long Spatial Information, a spatial range (e.g., specific link IDs, lane IDs and distances, or an equivalent representation) that corresponds to the lane reduction region for which an LC proposal section should be set (this is the “expected LC proposal section” for the test).
- Any other inputs required by the lane-change/navigation logic are in nominal states (no map errors, no LC suppression due to external constraints, and no ongoing route recalculation that would invalidate the Long Spatial Information).
fields.postconditions$599:
- For the evaluated scenario, the output LC Proposal Section (Internal) is set (non-empty / valid).
- The spatial extent and representation of LC Proposal Section (Internal) correspond to the lane-reduction-related portion of the route identified in the Long Spatial Information (the expected LC proposal section), such that:
     -The lane reduction point lies within, or is appropriately covered by, the LC Proposal Section (Internal).
     -No unrelated, non–lane-reduction route segments are incorrectly marked as part of the LC Proposal Section (Internal).
-The LC Proposal Section (Internal) can be used downstream as the “LC proposal section (Auto section) for lane reductions” as required by the specification.

testCaseSteps.action: Configure the navigation system with a specific test route from the current vehicle position to a chosen destination such that, according to the map data, there is a lane reduction ahead on the route (for example, a segment where the current lane terminates or the number of lanes decreases). Ensure that the Long Spatial Information (MapService) contains lane-level information for this area, including the exact location and extent of the lane reduction. From this Long Spatial Information, identify and document the spatial range (e.g., link IDs, lane IDs and distances, or equivalent) that represents the lane reduction region where an LC proposal section is expected.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: The configured route and Long Spatial Information clearly show at least one lane reduction in the direction of travel, and the lane reduction region is unambiguously defined and documented as the expected LC proposal section for this test. The Long Spatial Information is complete and valid for all segments needed to cover the lane reduction region.
testCaseSteps.notes: This step establishes a controlled scenario where a lane reduction is present in the Long Spatial Information, allowing the test to clearly define what the expected LC proposal section for lane reduction should be.

testCaseSteps.action: Start or continue system execution with the configured route active and position the vehicle (or ego position in simulation) upstream of the lane reduction region, at a point where the Long Spatial Information (MapService) already covers the full lane reduction region. Allow the system to process the Long Spatial Information and reach a steady operating state for this route and position without introducing faults or configuration changes.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: After processing the current route and Long Spatial Information, the navigation and lane-change logic has all necessary map context, including recognition that a lane reduction exists ahead on the route. Internally, the logic responsible for establishing the LC Proposal Section (Internal) has sufficient information to determine an LC proposal section associated with the lane reduction region.
testCaseSteps.notes: This step ensures that the system has had enough time and data to interpret the Long Spatial Information and detect the lane reduction, so that any LC proposal section for lane reduction can be properly set before observation.

testCaseSteps.action: Once the system has reached a stable state for the configured route and ego position, read or log the output LC Proposal Section (Internal). Decode or interpret this signal according to its defined structure (for example, using start and end positions along the route, a list of link IDs, lane IDs, or other spatial representation used for LC Proposal Section (Internal)).
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: The LC Proposal Section (Internal) output is present and represents a specific section along the route; it is not empty, defaulted, or in an error state. The spatial representation of LC Proposal Section (Internal) (such as its start and end positions or sequence of links) can be clearly interpreted and is suitable for comparison with the expected lane reduction region derived from the Long Spatial Information.
testCaseSteps.notes: This step directly observes the LC Proposal Section (Internal) required by the specification so that it can be compared to the expected lane reduction section.

testCaseSteps.action: Compare the observed LC Proposal Section (Internal) with the expected lane reduction region documented from the Long Spatial Information. Check that the LC Proposal Section (Internal) covers the lane reduction point and that its spatial boundaries (for example, start and end along the route, or included links/lanes) are consistent with the lane-reduction-related segment of the route, without including unrelated upstream or downstream segments that are not associated with the lane reduction.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: The LC Proposal Section (Internal) matches the lane reduction region identified from the Long Spatial Information: the lane reduction point lies within the LC proposal section, and the section’s start and end are consistent with the expected coverage (for example, beginning sufficiently before the lane reduction and ending at or shortly after it, as defined by the design). No additional, unrelated route segments are incorrectly included in the LC Proposal Section (Internal). This confirms that the system has “set an LC proposal section for lane reductions” as required.
testCaseSteps.notes: This is the primary verification step that demonstrates the LC Proposal Section (Internal) is correctly established for lane reduction based on the Long Spatial Information.

testCaseSteps.action: Optionally repeat the above procedure with one or more additional test routes that contain lane reductions with different geometries or contexts (for example, lane reduction on the leftmost lane vs. rightmost lane, or multiple lane reductions in series), each time identifying the expected lane reduction region from the Long Spatial Information and comparing it with the observed LC Proposal Section (Internal).
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: For each additional route scenario with a lane reduction, the LC Proposal Section (Internal) is consistently set to correspond to the lane-reduction-related segment identified in the Long Spatial Information. In no case is LC Proposal Section (Internal) missing when a clear lane reduction exists on the route, nor is it set for segments where no lane reduction is present.
testCaseSteps.notes: This step provides broader coverage and confirms that the behavior of setting LC Proposal Section (Internal) for lane reductions is robust across different lane reduction patterns and route configurations, not just a single example.

fields.name: Traffic Jam Avoidance Lane Change – Proposal Generation for Mainline Destination
fields.description: Verify that, when the destination is on the mainline side and a traffic jam is expected ahead in the ego lane based on Long Spatial Information (MapService) and related traffic information, the software outputs LC Proposal Info (Internal) that represents a lane change proposal to avoid the traffic jam. This test is written at a conceptual level to match the current T.B.D. status of the detailed specification and may require refinement once the detailed section-setting rules and LC proposal data format are fixed.
fields.preconditions$599:
- The system is powered on and operating in a normal, fault-free condition.
- A valid navigation route has been set from the current vehicle position to a destination that lies on the mainline side (e.g., continuing straight on the mainline, not exiting to a ramp).
- The Long Spatial Information (MapService) and associated traffic information indicate that, in the ego lane on the current route, a traffic jam is expected ahead (for example, reduced speed and high density starting at a known position ahead along the ego lane), while an adjacent lane on the mainline side offers a less congested path toward the destination.
- The test designer has identified and documented:
     -The route portion ahead where the traffic jam is expected in the ego lane.
     -At least one feasible lane change into another lane that can avoid or significantly mitigate the traffic jam while still leading toward the destination.
- No other suppression conditions or higher-priority behaviors are active that would globally prevent lane change proposals (for example, no global LC suppression due to legal restrictions or system errors).
- Any configuration related to traffic-jam-based lane change proposals is enabled (if such configuration exists in the test environment).
fields.postconditions$599:
- For the evaluated scenario, the output LC Proposal Info (Internal):
- Is present and valid (i.e., not empty, not a “no proposal” value).
- Encodes a lane change proposal intended to avoid the detected or predicted traffic jam in the ego lane while proceeding toward the mainline-side destination (for example, via a designated target lane and a proposal type or reason that indicates traffic-jam avoidance).
- Is consistent with the route and traffic conditions indicated by the Long Spatial Information (MapService) (i.e., the proposed lane change leads to a less congested path that still progresses toward the destination).
- In the absence of the described traffic jam in the ego lane, no traffic-jam-avoidance-specific LC proposal is generated under otherwise equivalent route and destination conditions (this may be verified by an optional comparative scenario).

testCaseSteps.action: Configure the navigation system with a route from the current vehicle position to a destination that is located on the mainline side (i.e., the planned route continues along the mainline rather than exiting to a ramp or side road). Using the test tools or map scenario editor, set up the Long Spatial Information (MapService) and associated traffic information so that a traffic jam (e.g., low speed and high density) is expected ahead in the current ego lane while at least one adjacent lane on the mainline remains relatively free-flowing toward the destination. Document the spatial extent of the expected traffic jam and the candidate lane(s) that can be used to avoid it.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: The configured route and Long Spatial Information clearly represent a situation where the ego lane ahead is expected to be congested, and an adjacent lane on the mainline provides a less congested alternative path toward the destination. The location and extent of the expected traffic jam, as well as the candidate lane(s) for avoidance, are clearly documented for later comparison.
testCaseSteps.notes: This step creates a controlled scenario satisfying the high-level requirement: the destination is on the mainline side, and a traffic jam is expected ahead in the ego lane, with at least one viable alternative lane for avoidance.

testCaseSteps.action: Start or continue system execution with the above route active and position the vehicle (or ego position in simulation) at a point upstream of the beginning of the expected traffic jam region, such that the Long Spatial Information (MapService) already includes the upcoming jam segment and the adjacent lanes. Allow the system to process the map and traffic information and reach a steady state without injecting faults or changing configuration.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: After processing the map and route context, the lane-change/navigation logic has recognized both the mainline-side destination route and the presence of an expected traffic jam ahead in the ego lane. Internally, the system has sufficient information to determine whether a lane change to an alternative lane can avoid or mitigate the traffic jam while still leading toward the destination.
testCaseSteps.notes: This step ensures that all necessary information from Long Spatial Information and traffic data is available to the system at the time when a traffic-jam-avoidance LC proposal could be generated.

testCaseSteps.action: Once the system has reached a steady state for the configured route and ego position, read or log the output LC Proposal Info (Internal), including any structured data fields that indicate the presence, type, or reason of an LC proposal (for example, flags, proposal type enums, target lane information, or other attributes associated with a traffic-jam-avoidance lane change).
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: The LC Proposal Info (Internal) output is present and indicates that an LC proposal exists. The contents of LC Proposal Info (Internal) (e.g., proposal type, reason, or attribute) show that the proposal is specifically related to avoiding a traffic jam with a lane change, rather than being unrelated to congestion (such as a destination-only lane change with no congestion context). The signal is in a valid, non-error state.
testCaseSteps.notes: This step directly observes the LC proposal to avoid traffic jams that the requirement describes, at the level currently possible without a finalized detailed specification. The exact encoding of “traffic jam avoidance” may need to be refined once the detailed design is fixed.

testCaseSteps.action: Interpret the LC Proposal Info (Internal) output to determine the proposed target lane and the approximate spatial section where the lane change is intended to occur. Compare this with the documented traffic jam region and the identified candidate lane(s) from the Long Spatial Information. Check that the proposed lane change would move the ego vehicle away from the jammed lane into a lane that provides a less congested path toward the mainline-side destination.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: The LC Proposal Info (Internal) describes a lane change into a lane that avoids the expected traffic jam ahead in the ego lane. Specifically, the proposed target lane lies in a region where the traffic conditions are better than in the ego lane (e.g., higher expected speed, less congestion) and is aligned with the route toward the mainline-side destination. The proposed lane change is not into a lane that remains equally or more congested, nor into an exit or route that diverges from the destination.
testCaseSteps.notes: This step verifies that the LC proposal is not merely any lane change, but one that is consistent with traffic-jam avoidance and still leads toward the mainline-side destination, as described in the requirement.

testCaseSteps.action: Optionally, configure a comparative scenario using a similar route and destination but without an expected traffic jam in the ego lane (for example, by setting normal traffic conditions in the ego lane while keeping other conditions as similar as possible). Run the system to a comparable position and observe LC Proposal Info (Internal) in this no-jam scenario.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: In the comparative no-jam scenario, LC Proposal Info (Internal) does not contain a lane change proposal that is specifically marked or reasoned as “avoiding a traffic jam.” Either no LC proposal is generated, or any LC proposals that exist are unrelated to congestion avoidance (for example, they may be destination-related or lane-reduction-related according to other requirements). This contrast supports the interpretation that the LC proposal in the jam scenario is indeed triggered by traffic-jam-avoidance logic.
testCaseSteps.notes: This step increases confidence that the observed LC proposal in the jam scenario is due to the presence of an expected traffic jam in the ego lane, in line with the requirement intent, rather than being coincidental or due to unrelated conditions.

fields.name: Traffic Jam Avoidance Lane Change – No Proposal When Jam Condition Not Met
fields.description: Verify that when the traffic jam avoidance condition is not satisfied—for example, when no traffic jam is expected ahead in the ego lane or when the destination is not on the mainline side—the software does not output a traffic‑jam‑avoidance‑specific lane change proposal in LC Proposal Info (Internal), even though navigation is active. This ensures that traffic‑jam‑avoidance LC proposals are not generated outside their intended conditions, consistent with the requirement intent and the current T.B.D. detailed specification status.
fields.preconditions$599:
- The system is powered on and operating in a normal, fault-free condition.
- A valid navigation route is set and the system is in a state where navigation‑based lane changes could, in principle, be considered (navigation active, route fixed, no global LC suppression).
- At least one of the following is true for the configured scenario:
     - No traffic jam is expected ahead in the ego lane, according to the Long Spatial Information (MapService) and associated traffic information (e.g., normal/free-flow speeds with no significant congestion markers), while the destination may be on the mainline side; or
     - The destination is not on the mainline side (e.g., the route will exit to a ramp or branch), even if some traffic slowdown exists in the ego lane, such that the conditions described in the requirement (“destination is on the mainline side and traffic jam is expected ahead in the ego lane”) are not fully satisfied.
- Any configuration relating specifically to traffic‑jam‑avoidance LC proposals is enabled so that if the jam condition were present, proposals could be generated (i.e., we are only removing the jam/destination condition, not disabling the feature).
- No external faults or test harness overrides are suppressing all LC proposals system‑wide.
fields.postconditions$599:
- For the evaluated scenario(s) where the requirement’s traffic jam avoidance preconditions are not met, the output LC Proposal Info (Internal):
     - Does not contain a lane change proposal whose purpose or reason is “avoiding a traffic jam” in the ego lane.
     - Either contains no LC proposal at all or only proposals clearly attributable to other behaviors (for example, destination‑based LC, lane‑reduction‑based LC, or other navigation behaviors defined in separate requirements).
- No evidence is observed that the system proposes a lane change under the label, type, or reason of “traffic jam avoidance” when the requirement’s mainline‑destination plus ego‑lane‑jam condition is not satisfied.

testCaseSteps.action: Configure a first scenario in the navigation system where the route from the current vehicle position to the destination is on the mainline side (the route continues along the mainline), but the Long Spatial Information (MapService) and associated traffic information indicate no traffic jam ahead in the ego lane (for example, normal speeds and no congestion flags). Keep other conditions (e.g., road geometry, adjacent lanes) similar to the jam scenario used in the positive test if possible.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: The configured route is active and valid, with the destination on the mainline side. The Long Spatial Information and traffic data show normal traffic conditions in the ego lane over the same general region where a jam was configured in the positive test, ensuring that the only intended difference is the absence of the traffic jam condition.
testCaseSteps.notes: This scenario isolates the absence of the “traffic jam expected in ego lane” condition while keeping other navigation conditions similar, so that any difference in LC Proposal Info (Internal) can be attributed to the traffic jam condition.

testCaseSteps.action: Start or continue system execution with this non‑jam mainline route active and position the vehicle (or ego position in simulation) upstream of the region analogous to where a jam would be, ensuring that the Long Spatial Information (MapService) for this region is already available to the system. Allow the system to process the map and traffic information and reach a steady state.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: The lane‑change/navigation logic has processed the route and traffic information and recognizes that the destination is on the mainline side but that no significant traffic jam exists ahead in the ego lane. The system is in a state where it could generate an LC proposal if the traffic jam avoidance conditions were met, but those specific conditions are not present.
testCaseSteps.notes: This step ensures that the system has all relevant route context but is explicitly missing the key “traffic jam in ego lane” trigger condition from the requirement.

testCaseSteps.action: Once the system is in a steady state, read or log LC Proposal Info (Internal) for this scenario, including any data fields that specify proposal type, reason, or attributes (such as “traffic jam avoidance,” destination LC, lane reduction LC, etc.).
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: LC Proposal Info (Internal) does not contain a lane change proposal that is marked or identifiable as being for traffic jam avoidance. Either there is no LC proposal at all, or any LC proposals that exist are clearly associated with other purposes (for example, destination‑based LC or lane‑reduction‑based LC) and not tagged or reasoned as congestion‑avoidance proposals.
testCaseSteps.notes: This step verifies that the absence of a traffic jam in the ego lane prevents the generation of a traffic‑jam‑avoidance LC proposal, even though navigation is active and the destination is on the mainline side.

testCaseSteps.action: Configure a second scenario where a traffic jam (congestion) is represented in the map/traffic information somewhere along the route, but the destination is not on the mainline side (for example, the planned route requires the vehicle to exit to a ramp or branch). Ensure that the traffic jam is located in the ego lane along a segment that is not consistent with the “destination on the mainline side” condition described in the requirement.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: The configured route and Long Spatial Information show that the destination is reached by exiting the mainline, and a traffic jam exists in the ego lane on a part of the route that does not match the “mainline‑side destination” scenario. The conditions described in the requirement (“destination is on the mainline side and traffic jam is expected ahead in the ego lane”) are therefore not fully satisfied.
testCaseSteps.notes: This scenario isolates the absence of the “destination is on the mainline side” condition while allowing some congestion to exist, to confirm that both destination and jam conditions together are necessary for a traffic‑jam‑avoidance LC proposal.

testCaseSteps.action: Run the system with this non‑mainline‑destination route active and position the ego vehicle upstream of the jam region so that the Long Spatial Information (MapService) including the jam is available. Allow the system to process the information and reach a steady state, then read or log LC Proposal Info (Internal).
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: In this scenario, LC Proposal Info (Internal) again does not contain any lane change proposal that is clearly labeled or reasoned as “avoiding a traffic jam.” If LC proposals exist, they correspond to other behaviors (for example, lane change to prepare for the exit) and are not identified as traffic‑jam‑avoidance proposals.
testCaseSteps.notes: This step verifies that a traffic jam alone, without the destination being on the mainline side, does not trigger the traffic‑jam‑avoidance LC proposal logic described in the requirement.

testCaseSteps.action: Compare the observations from these non‑jam / non‑mainline scenarios with the positive scenario (where the destination is on the mainline side and a traffic jam is expected in the ego lane). Confirm that only when both the mainline destination and ego‑lane traffic jam conditions are present does LC Proposal Info (Internal) contain a traffic‑jam‑avoidance lane change proposal.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: The comparative analysis shows a clear pattern: in scenarios where the requirement’s conditions are not satisfied (no jam in ego lane and/or destination not on mainline side), LC Proposal Info (Internal) does not contain a traffic‑jam‑avoidance LC proposal, while in the positive scenario where all conditions are met, such a proposal is present. This supports the conclusion that traffic‑jam‑avoidance LC proposals are generated only under the intended conditions.
testCaseSteps.notes: This step ties together positive and negative scenarios to demonstrate that the system behavior aligns with the requirement intent and avoids generating traffic‑jam‑avoidance LC proposals outside of the specified conditions, even though the detailed spec is still T.B.D.

fields.name: Calculate and output acceleration and jerk values from arbitrated acceleration profile
fields.description:
Verify that LoMP correctly calculates 5 output values from the arbitrated acceleration profile, applies SP_2 checks to target acceleration, and outputs all values externally.

 

SWRD-LoMP-Arbitration_Calculation_ControlCommandValue_0001_SP_1
fields.preconditions$599:
Input: ArbitratedAccelerationProfile 
SP_2 rule definition is available (e.g., acceleration limits, smoothness constraints).
Output destinations from LoMP are defined and accessible for validation.
fields.postconditions$599:
LoMP external outputs contain all 5 computed values.
No missing or default placeholder values unless profile is empty.
No stale data — outputs reflect latest profile cycle.

testCaseSteps.action: Access the arbitrated acceleration profile for the current calculation cycle.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Retrieved profile contains valid acceleration/time data points for the required computation period.

testCaseSteps.action: Extract the target acceleration value from the profile for the current time step or relevant point.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Raw target acceleration value is derived from profile data.

testCaseSteps.action: Compare TargetAcceleration against SP_2 limits (e.g., range limits, safety smoothness rules).
testCaseSteps.expectedResult:
If within limits → retain raw value.
If outside limits → adjust (clip or smooth) to comply with SP_2.

testCaseSteps.action:
Determine jerk value for driving increase: rate of change in acceleration during increase phases:
Jerk = Accel / Time
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Value computed in m/s³ using profile transitions where acceleration increased.

testCaseSteps.action: Determine jerk value for driving decrease phases using the same formula but for decreases in acceleration.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Value computed in m/s³ using profile transitions where acceleration decreased.

testCaseSteps.action: Determine jerk value for braking increase phases from profile when braking becomes stronger (more negative acceleration).
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Value computed in m/s³ for negative acceleration changes in braking increase phase.

testCaseSteps.action: Determine jerk value when braking is reduced (negative acceleration magnitude decreases).
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Value in m/s³ representing reduction of braking force over time.

testCaseSteps.action: Send all 5 values (TargetAcceleration, DrivingIncreaseJerk, DrivingDecreaseJerk, BrakingIncreaseJerk, BrakingDecreaseJerk) to LoMP’s external interface.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult:
All outputs populated with computed or adjusted values.
Units correct: m/s² for acceleration, m/s³ for jerk.

testCaseSteps.action: Validate that all outputs meet SP_2 (for target acceleration) and are present for external consumption.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult:
Output interface contains latest cycle’s values.
No stale or missing data.

fields.name: Verify correct calculation and output when target acceleration equals SP_2 upper limit.
fields.description:
Verify that LoMP correctly calculates 5 output values from the arbitrated acceleration profile that are at the maximum value allowed, applies SP_2 checks to target acceleration, and outputs all values externally.

 

SWRD-LoMP-Arbitration_Calculation_ControlCommandValue_0001_SP_1
fields.preconditions$599:
System constants & limits from configuration:
SP_2_TargetAccel_UpperLimit = 4.0 m/s²
SP_2_TargetAccel_LowerLimit = -5.0 m/s²
Jerk_LowerLimit = 0.0 m/s³
Jerk_UpperLimit = 5.0 m/s³
Input:
ArbitratedAccelerationProfile contains a current acceleration value = 4.0 m/s² at the evaluation time step.
All jerk values in profile are within limits (no clamping expected).
LoMP output interface is functional.
fields.postconditions$599:
TargetAcceleration output = 4.0 m/s² (unchanged — matches upper limit exactly).
Calculated jerk values are output unchanged, as they are within configured jerk limits.
All outputs satisfy SP_2 and jerk constraints.
External systems receive values in correct units and in current cycle.

testCaseSteps.action: Retrieve ArbitratedAccelerationProfile for the current calculation cycle.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Profile data is available and contains valid acceleration/jerk points.

testCaseSteps.action: Identify the current time step acceleration value from profile = 4.0 m/s².
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Value is exactly at SP_2 upper limit.

testCaseSteps.action:
if TargetAcceleration > 4.0 → clamp
if TargetAcceleration < -5.0 → clamp
else → keep unchanged
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Since 4.0 equals upper limit, value remains unchanged.

testCaseSteps.action: Compute DrivingIncreaseJerk, DrivingDecreaseJerk, BrakingIncreaseJerk, BrakingDecreaseJerk from profile change rates.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: All jerk values are within [0.0, 5.0] m/s³ and remain unchanged.

testCaseSteps.action: Send calculated TargetAcceleration and all jerk values to LoMP external interface.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult:
TargetAcceleration = 4.0 m/s² exactly.
All jerk values match calculated values from profile.

testCaseSteps.action: Check LoMP output registers/logs for this cycle.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Outputs match expected values and satisfy SP_2 & jerk limit rules.

testCaseSteps.action: Determine jerk value when braking is reduced (negative acceleration magnitude decreases).
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Value in m/s³ representing reduction of braking force over time.

fields.name: Clamp target acceleration and recalculate jerk values when input exceeds SP_2 upper limit.
fields.description:
Verify that LoMP correctly calculates 5 output values from the arbitrated acceleration profile that are initially outside the value allowed, applies SP_2 checks to target acceleration, and outputs all values externally.

 

SWRD-LoMP-Arbitration_Calculation_ControlCommandValue_0001_SP_1
fields.preconditions$599:
System constants & limits from configuration:
SP_2_TargetAccel_UpperLimit = 4.0 m/s²
SP_2_TargetAccel_LowerLimit = -5.0 m/s²
Jerk_LowerLimit = 0.0 m/s³
Jerk_UpperLimit = 5.0 m/s³
Input:
ArbitratedAccelerationProfile contains a current time step acceleration value = 4.5 m/s² (exceeds the upper limit).
Associated jerk values are still within configured jerk limits.
LoMP output interface is functional.
fields.postconditions$599:
TargetAcceleration output is clamped to 4.0 m/s² (SP_2 upper limit).
All jerk values are recalculated based on the clamped target acceleration.
Final outputs satisfy SP_2 and jerk constraints before being published externally.
Output is sent in correct units and in the same control cycle.

testCaseSteps.action: Retrieve ArbitratedAccelerationProfile for the current calculation cycle.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Profile data is available and contains valid acceleration/jerk points.

testCaseSteps.action:
Compare raw TargetAcceleration (4.5 m/s²) to configured SP_2 limits:

if > 4.0 m/s² → set to 4.0 m/s²
if < -5.0 m/s² → set to -5.0 m/s²
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Raw value exceeds upper limit → clamped to 4.0 m/s².

testCaseSteps.action:
Using clamped TargetAcceleration, recompute:
DrivingIncreaseJerk
DrivingDecreaseJerk
BrakingIncreaseJerk
BrakingDecreaseJerk
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: All output jerk values are within range, clamped only if necessary.

testCaseSteps.action: Ensure each jerk is within [0.0, 5.0] m/s³; clamp if exceeded.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: All output jerk values are within range, clamped only if necessary.

testCaseSteps.action: Publish clamped TargetAcceleration and recalculated jerks to LoMP’s external interface.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: TargetAcceleration = 4.0 m/s² exactly; jerk values updated; outputs available externally in same cycle.

testCaseSteps.action: Inspect output registers/logs for this control cycle.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Accelerations and jerks satisfy SP_2 and jerk limits; no error handling needed beyond clamping.

fields.name: Limit Target Acceleration within jerk-based bounds based on acceleration sign rules.
fields.description:
Ensure the target acceleration is limited within bounds calculated using the previous target acceleration and the applicable jerk values.
Select the appropriate jerk type (braking or driving) depending on the sign of the target acceleration and the previous target acceleration.

 

SWRD-LoMP-Arbitration_Calculation_ControlCommandValue_0001_SP_2
fields.preconditions$599:
Inputs available:
TargetAccel_Calc — calculated target acceleration before limitation (m/s²).
TargetAccel_Prev — previous cycle’s target acceleration (m/s²).
DrivingIncreaseJerk — jerk limit for acceleration increase in driving mode (m/s³).
DrivingDecreaseJerk — jerk limit for acceleration decrease in driving mode (m/s³).
BrakingIncreaseJerk — jerk limit for acceleration increase in braking mode (m/s³).
BrakingDecreaseJerk — jerk limit for acceleration decrease in braking mode (m/s³).
Units:
Acceleration in m/s².
Jerk in m/s³.
Sign rule for jerk selection:
Use braking jerk limits if TargetAccel_Calc < 0.0 OR TargetAccel_Prev < 0.0.
Otherwise use driving jerk limits.
fields.postconditions$599:
The recorded TargetAcceleration value is not greater than UpperLimit and not less than LowerLimit.
TargetAcceleration has been calculated using the correct jerk type (driving or braking) based on sign rules.
All calculations preserve units: m/s² for acceleration, m/s³ for jerk.
Downstream modules receive the updated limited target acceleration in the same cycle.
No error flags are raised unless input data is missing or invalid.

testCaseSteps.action:
Compare TargetAccel_Calc and TargetAccel_Prev with 0.0 m/s².
If either is negative → select braking jerk limits.
Else → select driving jerk limits.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: ApplicableIncreaseJerk and ApplicableDecreaseJerk assigned from correct jerk type set.

testCaseSteps.action: UpperLimit = TargetAccel_Prev + ApplicableIncreaseJerk
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Upper limit correctly computed using the selected applicable increase jerk value.

testCaseSteps.action: LowerLimit = TargetAccel_Prev - ApplicableDecreaseJerk
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Lower limit correctly computed using the selected applicable decrease jerk value.

testCaseSteps.action:
If TargetAccel_Calc > UpperLimit → set to UpperLimit.
If TargetAccel_Calc < LowerLimit → set to LowerLimit.
Else → keep TargetAccel_Calc unchanged.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Limited target acceleration value is within [LowerLimit, UpperLimit].

testCaseSteps.action: Send the final limited target acceleration to downstream modules.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Output value reflects jerk-limited acceleration in compliance with requirement rules.

fields.name: Limit Target Acceleration using vehicle-specific jerk parameters.
fields.description:
Ensure that:

  1. The target acceleration calculated up to this point is limited according to vehicle-specific jerk values.
  2. The jerk values come from the correct jerk map (common or vehicle-specific).
  3. The limited target acceleration satisfies SP_2 rules.
  4. Map values are changeable based on towing control enable flag, calibration map info, and ACC drive mode (future-proof).

SWRD-LoMP-Arbitration_Calculation_ControlCommandValue_0001_SP_3
fields.preconditions$599:
Inputs:
TargetAccel_Calc (m/s²) — target acceleration before limitation.
Jerk map values:
DrivingIncreaseJerk
DrivingDecreaseJerk
BrakingIncreaseJerk
BrakingDecreaseJerk
TowingControlEnableFlag (boolean)
CalibrationMapInfo (data source)
ACCDriveMode (mode enum/string)
fields.postconditions$599:
Target acceleration is within jerk-bound limits from vehicle-specific map.
Correct jerk type was selected (driving or braking) based on sign rules.
Map values used are from correct source (common or vehicle-specific map).
Target acceleration satisfies SP_2 constraints.
Output published externally in correct units and accessible in the same cycle.
System state ready for next calculation cycle without retaining stale values.

testCaseSteps.action:
Evaluate TowingControlEnableFlag, CalibrationMapInfo, and ACCDriveMode.
If conditions require specific vehicle map → load that jerk map.
Else use current common jerk map.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Correct map values loaded for all jerk types (Driving Increase, Driving Decrease, Braking Increase, Braking Decrease).

testCaseSteps.action:
Evaluate sign of TargetAccel_Calc and previous target acceleration (TargetAccel_Prev):
If either < 0 m/s² → use braking jerk values.
Else → use driving jerk values.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Applicable Increase and Decrease Jerk values selected from loaded jerk map.

testCaseSteps.action:
UpperLimit = TargetAccel_Prev + ApplicableIncreaseJerk
LowerLimit = TargetAccel_Prev - ApplicableDecreaseJerk
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Bounds computed correctly in m/s².

testCaseSteps.action:
If TargetAccel_Calc > UpperLimit → set to UpperLimit.
If TargetAccel_Calc < LowerLimit → set to LowerLimit.
Else keep unchanged.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Output acceleration clamped to within [LowerLimit, UpperLimit].

testCaseSteps.action: Check limited TargetAcceleration against SP_2 constraints (safety/performance rules).
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Limited acceleration meets SP_2 — no violations of range or transition smoothness.

testCaseSteps.action: Send the final limited TargetAcceleration to LoMP’s external interface for downstream control.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Output available in current calculation cycle, correct units, and updated from limitation logic.

fields.name: Limit target acceleration to 0.0 m/s² when above threshold, unless acceleration-side enable flag is true
fields.description:
Ensure that:

  1. If TargetAccel_Calc > 0.0 m/s² and the acceleration-side enable flag is false, the target acceleration is limited to 0.0 m/s².
  2. If the acceleration-side enable flag is true, the limitation is not applied (target acceleration remains as calculated).
  3. Logic behaves consistently across valid and edge cases.

 

SWRD-LoMP-Arbitration_Calculation_ControlCommandValue_0001_SP_4
fields.preconditions$599:
Inputs:
TargetAccel_Calc — target acceleration before limitation (m/s²).
AccelSideEnableFlag — acceleration-side target acceleration enable flag (boolean).
Constants:
UPPER_LIMIT_ACCEL = 0.0 m/s² (fixed per requirement).
System capable of performing comparison and clamping logic in current control cycle.
Units:
Acceleration values measured in m/s².
fields.postconditions$599:
If AccelSideEnableFlag = true, post-limitation value equals original TargetAccel_Calc.
If AccelSideEnableFlag = false:
TargetAccel_Calc > 0.0, final output = 0.0 m/s².
TargetAccel_Calc ≤ 0.0, final output = unchanged from input.
Target acceleration output is correctly updated for consumption by next system stage.
All output values are in m/s² and valid for current control cycle.

testCaseSteps.action: Obtain TargetAccel_Calc and AccelSideEnableFlag from input signals.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Inputs retrieved correctly for current cycle.

testCaseSteps.action:
Evaluate AccelSideEnableFlag:
If true → skip limitation.
If false → proceed to limitation check.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Correct branching based on flag value.

testCaseSteps.action:
If AccelSideEnableFlag == False, check

If TargetAccel_Calc > UPPER_LIMIT_ACCEL (0.0 m/s²)
    TargetAccel_Limited = 0.0 m/s²
else
    TargetAccel_Limited = TargetAccel_Calc
testCaseSteps.expectedResult:
For values above 0.0 → capped to 0.0 m/s².
For values ≤ 0.0 → unchanged.

testCaseSteps.action: Send TargetAccel_Limited to output interface for downstream modules.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Output reflects limitation rules applied in this cycle.

fields.name: Limit negative target acceleration to counteract brake operation noise.
fields.description:
Ensure that:

  1. If TargetAccel_Calc is negative and AlarmRequestFlag is false, apply brake noise countermeasure limitation.
  2. If AlarmRequestFlag is true, skip limitation entirely.
  3. Calculate the brake noise countermeasure target acceleration correctly from previous target acceleration and reduction limit value.
  4. Determine reduction limit value correctly from min(3.5 m/s³, GuardMap value).
  5. Final limited target acceleration equals max(BrakeNoiseCountermeasureAccel, TargetAccel_Calc).

SWRD-LoMP-Arbitration_Calculation_ControlCommandValue_0001_SP_5
fields.preconditions$599:
Inputs:
TargetAccel_Calc (m/s²) — target acceleration before limitation.

If AlarmRequestFlag = true → TargetAccel_Limited == TargetAccel_Calc (no changes).
If AlarmRequestFlag = false AND TargetAccel_Calc < 0:
Reduction limit value correctly computed.
BrakeNoiseCountermeasureAccel = TargetAccel_Prev − ReductionLimitValue.
TargetAccel_Limited = max(BrakeNoiseCountermeasureAccel, TargetAccel_Calc).
Target acceleration meets the brake noise countermeasure rule and remains within safe limits.
Outputs updated in current calculation cycle, ready for use by downstream functions.

testCaseSteps.action: Retrieve TargetAccel_Calc, TargetAccel_Prev, GuardMapValue, and AlarmRequestFlag.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Inputs are valid for current calculation cycle.

testCaseSteps.action: If AlarmRequestFlag = true → skip limitation; set TargetAccel_Limited = TargetAccel_Calc.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Limitation process bypassed when flag is true.

testCaseSteps.action:
If AlarmRequestFlag = false:
Check if TargetAccel_Calc < 0.0.
If true → proceed with brake noise limitation logic.
If false → skip this limitation; output = TargetAccel_Calc.
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Limitation applies only to negative target acceleration values when alarm flag is false.

testCaseSteps.action: ReductionLimitValue = min(MaxReductionLimitConst, GuardMapValue)
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Reduction limit calculated correctly in m/s³ from the smaller of 3.5 or GuardMap value.

testCaseSteps.action: BrakeNoiseCountermeasureAccel = TargetAccel_Prev - ReductionLimitValue
testCaseSteps.expectedResult: Value in m/s² representing a softened deceleration target to reduce brake noise.

testCaseSteps.action: TargetAccel_Limited = max(BrakeNoiseCountermeasureAccel, TargetAccel_Calc)
testCaseSteps.expectedResult:

Chooses the “gentler” limit between noise countermeasure target and original calculation.

fields.name: Setting ODD violation state when in shoulder lane
fields.description: When the ego vehicle is driving within, entering, or exiting a shoulder lane, PlannerCore shall set the "ODD violation state" to kOddViolationDrivingOffRoadway, where "entering" and "exiting" align with the definition contained within SWRD-LaDSC-3.
fields.rationale$589: If the vehicle is driving on the shoulder lane, it is determined to be not in normal driving mode, and a state transition in the AD control system is carried out.

fields.name: Setting ODD violation state when not in shoulder lane
fields.description: When the ego vehicle is not driving within, entering, or exiting a shoulder lane, PlannerCore shall set the "ODD violation state" to kOddViolationNotSystemLimitation, where "entering" and "exiting" align with the definition contained within SWRD-LaDSC-3.
fields.rationale$589: Because no ODD violation state other than kOddViolationDrivingOffRoadway exists, any time that the ego vehicle is not within, entering, or exiting a shoulder, the ODD violation state should be reset to "no violation".

fields.name: Consistency between trajectory waypoints and yaw angle
fields.description:
PlannerCore shall output a trajectory whose path as defined by the coordinate waypoints is mutually consistent with the yaw angle, where mutually consistent is defined as follows:

 

For each trajectory point i, where (0 ≤ i ≤ 49), the yaw angle in the trajectory is within TBD [rad] of the yaw angle calculated from the path θi, where

θi = atan2(yi+1 − yi, xi+1 − xi)
fields.rationale$589: SWRD-PnP-LK-12_SP_1 requires that the path waypoints and yaw angles of the trajectory sent from IPA to downstream components are mutually consistent to comply with their design.

fields.name: Consistency between trajectory waypoints and velocity
fields.description:
PlannerCore shall output a trajectory whose path as defined by the coordinate waypoints is mutually consistent with the velocity, where mutually consistent is defined as follows:

 

For each trajectory point i, where (0 ≤ i ≤ 49), the velocity in the trajectory is within TBD [m/s] of the velocity calculated from the path vi, where

Δsi = √( (xi+1 − xi)2 + (yi+1 − yi)2 )
vi = Δsi / Δt
fields.rationale$589: SWRD-PnP-LK-12_SP_1 requires that the path waypoints and velocities of the trajectory sent from IPA to downstream components are mutually consistent to comply with their design.

fields.name: Consistency between trajectory waypoints and curvature
fields.description:
PlannerCore shall output a trajectory whose path as defined by the coordinate waypoints is mutually consistent with the curvature, where mutually consistent is defined as follows:

 

For each trajectory point i, where (1 ≤ i ≤ 49), the curvature in the trajectory is within TBD [m-1] of the curvature calculated from the path κi, where

κi = 2( (xi − xi−1)(yi+1 − yi−1) − (yi − yi−1)(xi+1 − xi−1) ) / (di−1,i ⋅ di,i+1 ⋅ di−1,i+1)

da,b = √( (xb − xa)2 + (yb − ya)2 )
fields.rationale$589: SWRD-PnP-LK-12_SP_1 requires that the path waypoints and curvatures of the trajectory sent from IPA to downstream components are mutually consistent to comply with their design.

fields.name: Consistency between trajectory waypoints and acceleration
fields.description:
PlannerCore shall output a trajectory whose path as defined by the coordinate waypoints is mutually consistent with the acceleration, where mutually consistent is defined as follows:

 

For each trajectory point i, where (0 ≤ i ≤ 48), the acceleration in the trajectory is within TBD [m/s2] of the acceleration calculated from the path ai, where

ai = (vi+1 − vi) / Δt
fields.rationale$589: SWRD-PnP-LK-12_SP_1 requires that the path waypoints and accelerations of the trajectory sent from IPA to downstream components are mutually consistent to comply with their design.

fields.name: Trajectory length and timestep
fields.description: PlannerCore shall output a trajectory that is a sequence of 51 points sampled at intervals of 0.1 s covering a time horizon from 0.0 seconds at point 0 to 5.0 seconds at the final point.
fields.rationale$589: SWRD-PnP-LK-12_SP_2 requires that the trajectory sent from IPA to the downstream components has this length with this timestep.

fields.name: Lateral Acceleration Limit for C-SPM
fields.description: PlannerCore shall generate a trajectory with target speeds such that the lateral acceleration at each trajectory point as defined in the Appendix: Definition_of_Common_equations does not exceed 3.0 m/s².
fields.rationale$589: Satisfies the requirements in UN R171 Section 5.3.7. The curvature requirement has been removed, meaning the lateral acceleration threshold applies at all times. This was done to better align with the implementation of PlannerCore, which checks lateral acceleration against the threshold regardless of curvature.

fields.name: Common Deceleration Operational Limit
fields.description: PlannerCore shall generate a trajectory such that the longitudinal acceleration at each trajectory point from t0 to t22 as defined in the Appendix: Definition_of_Common_equations is not less than alimit_min(v).
fields.rationale$589:
Comply with the minimum acceleration limit described in ISO15622 section 6.4.

Decomposition Note: This SCRD relates to SWRD-PnP-VF-Common_Operational_limits_SP_1.

fields.name: Common Acceleration Operational Limit
fields.description: PlannerCore shall generate a trajectory such that the longitudinal acceleration at each trajectory point from t0 to t22 as defined in the Appendix: Definition_of_Common_equations is not greater than alimit_max(v).
fields.rationale$589:
Comply with the minimum acceleration limit described in ISO15622 section 6.4.

Decomposition Note: This SCRD relates to SWRD-PnP-VF-Common_Operational_limits_SP_2.

fields.name: Common Deceleration Jerk Operational Limit
fields.description: PlannerCore shall generate a trajectory such that the longitudinal jerk at each trajectory point from t0 to t22 as defined in the Appendix: Definition_of_Common_equations is not less than jlimit_min(v).
fields.rationale$589:
Comply with the minimum acceleration limit described in ISO15622 section 6.4.
