fields.name: No LC suppression or rejection during active LC maneuver
fields.description:
Description: The Advanced Driver Planner shall apply no LC suppression or rejection action based on available space assessment during the Before Steering, LC 1st Half, or LC 2nd Half phases.

 

Rationale: The LC Condition table explicitly marks all in-progress LC phases (Before Steering, Lc1stHalf, Lc2ndHalf) as "-" (no action) for this feature. Once an LC is underway, space-availability suppression must not interrupt it, as doing so could cause unsafe mid-maneuver aborts.

 

Verification: Simulation

 

Category: Safety

fields.name: Traffic Flow LC Customization State
fields.description: The Advanced Driver Planner shall read the Non-Volatile Traffic Flow LC Custom State and use it to enable or suppress lane change proposals based on traffic flow. Lane change proposals influenced by traffic flow customization shall only be considered when the Custom State is On.

fields.name: Driver Confirmation with Blinker of System Requested Lane Change
fields.description:
The Advanced Driver Planner shall initiate a "Driver-Confirmed LC" assist and transition to the BeforeSteering state when all of the following conditions are simultaneously satisfied:

  • All Preconditions for Driver-Confirmed LC are currently met.
  • The AD State (ADStateManager) confirms that the system is in an active AD state eligible for LC assist.
  • The LC Proposal Display Status (HumanSystemIntegration) confirms that an LC proposal is currently being displayed to the driver.
  • InterComm (IOLayer) reports a valid Driver-Confirmed LC tap gesture on the left blinker or right blinker.

fields.name: DILC rejection when no available space for 10 seconds
fields.description:
Requirement: The Advanced Driver Planner shall reject a Driver-Initiated Lane Change request when no available LC space is detected in the target lane within 10.0 seconds, and the LC phase condition is "LCP inactive (Driver-Initiated)."

 

Rationale: 

SP_1 and the LC Condition table require that a Driver-Initiated LC is rejected (not merely suppressed) at the LCP inactive phase when no viable gap is projected to exist within the 10.0 s horizon. Rejecting early prevents the system from entering an LC sequence that cannot be safely completed.

 

Verification: Simulation or Unit Test

 

Category: Functional

fields.name: DCLC rejection when no available space for 20 seconds
fields.description:
Description: The Advanced Driver Planner shall suppress a Driver-Confirmed Lane Change proposal when no available LC space is detected in the target lane within 20.0 seconds, and the LC phase condition is "LCP inactive (Driver-Confirmed)."

 

Rationale: SP_2 and the LC Condition table require that a Driver-Confirmed LC proposal is suppressed (not proposed to the driver) when no viable gap is projected within the 20.0 s horizon. This complies with UN-R171 by ensuring proposals are only presented when LC is expected to be feasible.

 

Verification: Simulation

 

Category: Functional

fields.name: Measuring Steering Control Time
fields.description:
Description: The Advanced Driver Planner shall start measuring the LC steering control time from the moment the LC phase transitions from any phase other than Lc1stHalf into Lc1stHalf.

 

Rationale: SP_1 defines the start condition for the timeout timer as the transition into Lc1stHalf. Correct timer start anchoring is essential to ensure the 15.0 s threshold is evaluated from the true beginning of active steering control, not from request initiation or an earlier phase.

 

Verification: Simulation

 

Category: Functional

fields.name: Aborting Lane Change due to Long Lane Change Control Time
fields.description:
Description: The Advanced Driver Planner shall abort the Lane Change when the LC steering control time is greater than or equal to 15.0 seconds and the current Lane Change State is either Lc1stHalf or Lc2ndHalf.

 

Rationale: SP_1 and the LC Condition table specify that if LC control has not completed within 15.0 s of entering Lc1stHalf, the maneuver must be aborted on both Mainline and Branch scenarios. An LC that takes longer than this threshold is considered potentially unintended or unsafe and must not be allowed to continue.

 

Verification: Simulation

 

Category: Functional

fields.name: Ineligible states for LC steering control timeout LC abort
fields.description:
Description: The Advanced Driver Planner shall not apply the LC steering control timeout abort during the LCP Inactive (Driver-Initiated), LCP Inactive (Driver-Confirmed), or Before Steering LC phases.

 

Rationale: The LC Condition table explicitly marks all pre-steering phases as "-" (no action) for this feature. The timeout is only meaningful once active steering control has begun; applying it earlier could incorrectly abort LCs that have not yet started executing.

 

Verification: Simulation

 

Category: Functional

fields.name: LCP Inactive (Driver-Initiated) and Blinker in Opposite Direction
fields.description:
Description: The Advanced Driver Planner shall reject a Driver-Initiated LC when a blinker operation in the opposite direction to the LC direction is detected and the LC phase is LCP Inactive (Driver-Initiated) on Mainline.

 

Rationale: SP_1 and the LC Condition table specify a Reject action at the LCP Inactive (Driver-Initiated) / Mainline phase when an opposite-direction blinker is detected. An opposite blinker at this stage is interpreted as driver intent to cancel, and the LC request must be refused before any maneuver begins.

 

Verification: Simulation

 

Category: Functional

fields.name: LCP Inactive (Driver Confirmed) and Blinker in Opposite Direction
fields.description:
Description: The Advanced Driver Planner shall suppress a Driver-Confirmed LC proposal when a blinker operation in the opposite direction to the LC direction is detected and the LC phase is LCP Inactive (Driver-Confirmed).

 

Rationale: SP_1 and the LC Condition table specify a SuppressProposal action at the LCP Inactive (Driver-Confirmed) phase on both Mainline and Branch. Suppressing the proposal prevents the system from suggesting a LC that the driver has implicitly rejected by operating the opposite blinker.

 

Verification: Simulation

 

Category: Functional

fields.name: LC Outputs LC State Waiting Before Steering
fields.description: The Advanced Driver Planner shall output LC State value Waiting when the LC phase has not started steering.
fields.rationale$589: SP_1 requires LC State to be set to 3 (Waiting) during BeforeSteering to represent that the LC assist has been accepted and is pending steering initiation. ADP owns the LC phase state machine and is therefore responsible for generating this value.

fields.name: Output LC Direction Left When Left LC is requested but Before Steering
fields.description: The Advanced Driver Planner shall output LC Direction Left when the LC phase is BeforeSteering and the LC direction that has been requested is left.
fields.rationale$589: SP_1 requires LC Direction to reflect the active maneuver direction during BeforeSteering. ADP determines the LC direction as part of the LC planning decision and must make this available for downstream consumption.

fields.name: Output LC Direction Right When Right LC is requested but Before Steering
fields.description: The Advanced Drive Planner shall output LC Direction Right when the LC phase is has not started steering and the LC direction that has been requested is right.
fields.rationale$589: SP_1 requires LC Direction to reflect the active maneuver direction during BeforeSteering. A separate requirement for right direction ensures both directions are independently verifiable.

fields.name: LC Type output
fields.description:
The Advanced Drive Planner shall output the Lane Change Type when the lane change feature has not yet started steering but a lane change has been requested. Only one value at a time may be outputted. Values are:

  • Driver Initiated LC
  • Lane Change to Destination 
  • Lane Change due to Lane Reduction
  • Lane Change due to Branching
  • Lane Change due to Overtake
  • Lane Change due to return from Overtake
  • Lane Change out of Fastest Lane 
  • Lane Change due to Traffic Jam Avoidance
  • Lane Change due to End of Destination Traffic Jam
  • Lane Change due to Avoiding being Merged into
  • Lane Change due to Rear Yielding
  • Lane Change due to Avoiding the slow lane
fields.rationale$589: Advanced Driver Planner owns the LC type distinction and must correctly report the reason for a lane change so that the HMI system may display appropriate information to the driver.

fields.name: LC Steering Suppression Flag
fields.description: The Advanced Driver Planner shall output a Steering Suppression Flag value of true when the LC phase has been requested, and steering initiation is being suppressed.
fields.rationale$589: SP_2 requires the Steering Suppression Flag to be asserted during BeforeSteering whenever steering is being held back. ADP determines whether steering suppression is active and must generate this flag for the Intercom to forward to the HMI.

fields.name: LC Suppress Steering Reason
fields.description: The Advanced Drive Planner shall output the Steering Suppression Reason according to the active suppression condition defined in the Suppress Abort Conditions [Link TBD] details when the LC phase is BeforeSteering and steering initiation is being suppressed.
fields.rationale$589: SP_2 requires the Steering Suppression Reason to be populated based on the specific active suppress-steering condition. ADP owns the suppression condition evaluation and must encode the correct reason bits for the Intercom to relay to the HMI.

fields.name: Send Traffic Flow LC Customization State
fields.description: The InterComm subsystem shall read the raw switch state and detect when the driver has selected to disable Lane Change due to traffic flow and then send the status of the user selected Traffic Flow LC Custom State to the Advanced Driver Planner.

fields.name: Turn Indicator Stalk Position
fields.description:
InterCom subsystem shall detect and report the position of the turn indicator stalk. The possible positions are:

  • The Turn Switch Position (Left) First Position.
  • The Turn Switch Position (Left) Second Position.
  • The Turn Switch Position (Right) First Position.
  • The Turn Switch Position (Right) Second Position.
  • The Turn Switch Off Position 
  • The elapsed time the turn indicator stalk is in the left or right first position.

fields.name: LC Rejection Reason DILC
fields.description:
Description: The Intercom shall set the LC Rejection Data Reject Reason bit [6] (NoAvailableLcSpace) to true in the HumanSystemIntegration interface when the Advanced Driver Planner rejects a Driver-Initiated LC due to no available space in the target lane.

 

Rationale: SP_1 specifies that when a Driver-Initiated LC is rejected for this reason, the rejection reason code [6] (NoAvailableLcSpace) must be communicated via the HumanSystemIntegration interface, enabling the HMI to present the correct feedback to the driver.

 

Verification: Unit Test

 

Category: Information

fields.name: LC Rejection Reason DCLC
fields.description:
Description: The Intercom shall set the LC Proposal Data LC Proposal Suppression Reason bit [6] (NoAvailableLcSpace) to true in the HumanSystemIntegration interface when the Advanced Driver Planner suppresses a Driver-Confirmed LC proposal due to no available space in the target lane.

 

Rationale: SP_2 specifies that when a Driver-Confirmed LC proposal is suppressed for this reason, the suppression reason code [6] (NoAvailableLcSpace) must be set in the HumanSystemIntegration interface so the HMI can reflect the correct system state to the driver.

 

Verification: Unit Test

 

Category: Information

fields.name: Alert Driver of suppressed lane change due to steering control too long
fields.description:
Description: The Intercom shall set the following bits to true when LC is rejected due to the steering control timeout condition:

 

Rationale: SP_1 lists the LC Proposal Suppression Reason signal as a required output for this condition. Populating this reason code allows the HMI to correctly reflect why a proposal was withheld from the driver.

 

Verification: Bench Test

 

Category: Information

fields.name: SBR-11 Lane Change other than Merge or Branch
fields.description:
The scenario includes either the driver intentionally starts lane change by operating the turn signal or, system triggered starting lane change. Lane change and Merge scenarios differ in their necessity. A merge is a mandatory maneuver to maintain a physically or legally drivable path, whereas a lane change is optional. This means that if a lane change is unsuccessful, the ego vehicle can still continue in the flow of traffic.

 

[Expected behavior]*

Activating turn signal to appropriate direction ( or designated direction by driver**) , and confirming the traffic situation of the target lane for lane change.

After that, perform lateral movement smoothly.

Deactivating turn signal when the lateral movement  is completed.

 

*See Regulatory compliance as well because lane change behavior is restricted by the regulation.

 (UNR171 have some regularities for LCP:Lane Change Procedure and LCM: Lane Change Maneuver)

**See HMI requirement section for behavior that is related with human interaction (e.g. the timing of activate turn signal …etc)

These notes are inherited to sub-scenarios

fields.name: SBR-11-1 Driver-initiated Lane Change
fields.description:
This is a case where the driver initiates the lane change by turn signal operation. 

[Expected behavior]

Activating turn signal to designated direction by driver** , and confirming the traffic situation of the target lane for lane change.

After that, perform lateral movement smoothly.

Deactivating turn signal when the lateral movement  is completed.

 

**See HMI requirement section for behavior that is related with human interaction (e.g. the timing of activate turn signal …etc)

These notes are inherited to sub-scenarios

fields.name: SBR-11-2 Lane change to destination
fields.description:
Ego will perform necessary lane changes to reach its destination. This scenario is categorized under "Lane Change" rather than "Merge" because, even if the lane change fails, the vehicle can continue traveling, though it might miss the intended destination.

 

[Expected behavior]

Activate the turn signal in the appropriate direction for reaching the destination, and check the traffic conditions in the target lane before changing lanes.

Then, perform the lane change.

Deactivate the turn signal once the lane change is completed.

This sequence should be completed before reaching the branching section where continuing in the current lane would force the ego vehicle onto a different route which is not guided by navi.

fields.name: Timing Diagram
Minimum Scene Length
fields.description:
Requirement: The lane change scenes shall be a minimum of 25 seconds long, not including SUT warmup, unless noted otherwise in the sub scenario section below.

 

Rationale: 

The LC activation stage may take up to 10 seconds, and the LC maneuver may take up to 10 seconds. A 5 second period is included to look for the LC engagement command.

 

Documentation: 

Comment thread

fields.name: Timing of LC Command
fields.description:
Requirement: 

The scene shall include the Lane Change command two seconds after SUT engagement. 

 

Rationale: 

 

Just because a manual vehicle performed a Lane Change does not mean that the SIM vehicle will also perform a LC. The Lane Change maneuver must be requested for it to be a viable LC scene.
Additionally, the LC request ideally should not be repeated throughout the scene. I.e. We should not be targeting double Lane Changes. 


Lane_Change_Command topic still populates with command even if the LC will be denied by the feature. This will mean we capture driver initiated requests, and route-necessary LC requests.

 

Documentation: 

Conversation on Lane_Change_command topic being added to Mosaic.

fields.name: Autonomy Status of Collection Log[Best practice]
fields.description:
Best Practice Suggestion: 

The lane change scenes shall be collected while in autonomy.

 

Rationale 

This minimizes pose divergence concerns, especially since these scenes will be longer than other features’ scenes which increases the risk of the phenomenon.

fields.name: One LC request per scene
fields.description:
Requirement: 

The scene shall perform only one lane change request per scene. This includes system initiated lane change requests as well as driver initiated LC requests.

 

Rationale: 

 

At the time this requirement has been written, valuation is not robust enough to accurately triage two lane change maneuvers within the same scene.

 

A potential LC in sim is measured by either LC_status_output is populated with a non neutral value, OR vehicle report logs turn signal input.

fields.name: Collision status [best practice]
fields.description:
Requirements:

There shall be no ado-initiated collision in SIM. Collisions caused by ego are acceptable, but collisions caused by ado shall be removed.

 

Rationale: 

We don’t want scenes where the pose divergence is too great. If SIM is colliding with an ado, that’s a great indicator that mission isn’t recording data that is useful for us.

fields.description:
Requirement:

All scenes must be current on ODD.

 

Rationale:

fields.name: Lane Keeping - Stay in lane with discernible lane boundaries
fields.description:
REQUIREMENT STATEMENT

When driving in-lane with discernible lane boundaries, the ego vehicle SHALL be able to stay in lane by keeping distance dLB measured between the closest point of the ego vehicle's FOOTPRINT and the outer part of the LANE BOUNDARY.

 

With:

dLB ≥ 0  meter OR  dLB <  0 meter for less than 1 second.

 

RATIONALE

Why: Stay within safe boundaries 

Erroneous lane departure could lead to entering a potential collision zone

 

Thresholds:

Distance dLB: For basic in-lane driving with discernible left and right lane boundaries (lane marking or lane edge), the vehicle’s footprint is expected to never leave the lane boundaries. This is represented by a threshold of 0 meter.


Time: Outliers are tolerated for a short period of time to account for sensor, perception and localization inaccuracies/uncertainties. A time period of 1 second accounts for the expected reaction time of the safety driver.

fields.name: Lane Keeping - Stay in lane with indiscernible lane boundaries
fields.description:
REQUIREMENT STATEMENT

When driving in-lane with indiscernible lane boundaries (i.e. missing lane boundaries, lane splits, lane merges, intersections), the ego vehicle SHALL be able to stay in lane by keeping distance dLB measured between the closest point of the ego vehicle's FOOTPRINT and the outer part of the LANE BOUNDARY.

 

With:

dLB ≥ -0.1 meter OR  dLB <  -0.1 meter for less than 1 second

 

 

RATIONALE

Why: Stay within safe boundaries 

Erroneous lane departure could lead to entering a potential collision zone

 

Thresholds:

Distance dLB: For in-lane driving with indiscernible left or right lane boundaries, the vehicle’s footprint is expected to not leave the lane boundaries with more than the given threshold of -0.1 meter. This requirement allows a 10% higher margin than HSR1a. When centered in lane, ego has on average 0.8 meter on both sides available to deviate before reaching a lane boundary. Adding a 10% higher margin based on the available space results in 0.08 meters which will  be rounded to 0.1 meter. 


Time: Outliers are tolerated for a short period of time to account for sensor, perception and localization inaccuracies/uncertainties. A time period of 1 second accounts for the expected reaction time of the alert safety driver.

fields.name: Max speed limit
fields.description:
REQUIREMENT STATEMENT

The ego vehicle's speed vego SHALL ALWAYS be:

vego ≤ speed limit + 6 kph

 

 

RATIONALE

Why: Stay within safe boundaries and obeying traffic laws

 

Thresholds:

Speed margin: There is an additional margin of 6 kph applied to the speed limit to match the 20TM requirement. In 20TM, the actual (measured) speed is allowed to be up to 6 kph greater than the speed requested by the planner before a disengagement is triggered. In the case that the planner perfectly outputs the set speed, and that the set speed is constrained to be ≤ the speed limit (operationally or otherwise), this means the measured speed should never exceed the speed limit by > 6 kph.

 

Time: In accordance with the 20TM production requirement, outliers are not tolerated. Any speed above the threshold should result in a disengagement.

fields.name: Speed Limit Transitions
fields.description:
REQUIREMENT STATEMENT

The ego vehicle's speed vego SHALL ALWAYS be:

vego ≤ speed limit + 6 kph

 

WHERE the applicable speed limit is the minimum speed limit that touches any part of the ego vehicle’s FOOTPRINT.

 

 

RATIONALE

Why: Stay within safe boundaries and obeying traffic laws

 

Thresholds:

Speed margin: There is an additional margin of 6 kph applied to the speed limit to match the 20TM requirement. In 20TM, the actual (measured) speed is allowed to be up to 6 kph greater than the speed requested by the planner before a disengagement is triggered. In the case that the planner perfectly outputs the set speed, and that the set speed is constrained to be ≤ the speed limit (operationally or otherwise), this means the measured speed should never exceed the speed limit by > 6 kph.

 

Time: In accordance with the 20TM production requirement, outliers are not tolerated. Any speed above the threshold should result in a disengagement

 

Applicable speed limit: The ego vehicle’s speed is compared to the minimum speed limit that the ego vehicle’s footprint touches to ensure legal compliance. A new speed limit zone begins at the point that the sign is posted. As a result, slowing down after ego’s front bumper crosses the sign (if the speed limit is decreasing) or speeding up before ego’s rear bumper crosses the sign (if the speed limit is increasing) is technically speeding and should be avoided.

fields.name: ODD Speed Limit
fields.description:
REQUIREMENT STATEMENT

The ego vehicle's speed vego SHALL be:

vego ≤ ODD speed limit + 5 mph OR

vego > ODD speed limit + 5 mph for less or equal to 2 seconds 

 

With:

ODD speed limit = 70 mph (112.7kph)

 

RATIONALE

Why: Stay within safe boundaries

Comply with Safety Case

 

Thresholds:

Speed margin: Tolerating a 10% speed margin of the max ODD speed limit results in 5 mph (rounded to nearest multiple of 5). This also follows a common rule-of-thumb that allows for speed variations up to 5 mph over the speed limit.

 

Time: Outliers are tolerated for a short period of time to account for sensor inaccuracies and minor control overshooting. A time period of 2 seconds is given to provide the system enough time to correct the speed violation or the safety driver to intervene.

fields.name: Longitudinal Distance to Ado Vehicles Ahead in Lane
fields.description:
WIP. Update under way. Check V3 for previous version.

 

 

 

 

 

REQUIREMENT STATEMENT

While the Ego vehicle is driving in lane, merging, or lane‑changing into an adjacent lane, the Ego vehicle SHALL maintain a longitudinal distance greater than or equal to dₘᵢₙ between the closest point of the Ego vehicle footprint and the footprint of any Ado vehicle that the Ego vehicle laterally overlaps.

If the behavior of an Ado vehicle from an adjacent lane results in a longitudinal distance less than dₘᵢₙ (e.g., a cut‑in event), HSR4a applies until the longitudinal distance is again greater than or equal to dₘᵢₙ.

 

1. Gap Definition:

 

 

gap(t) = xLV(t) - xEgo(t)
 

where t = 0 is the time at which the Lead Vehicle begins braking.
 

2. All-Times Minimum Gap Safety Condition:


The minimum distance dₘᵢₙ is defined such that, in case of a driver takeover braking event, the bumper to bumper gap satisfies:

 This condition must hold for the entire duration of the braking event, from the onset of Lead Vehicle braking until both vehicles come to rest.

 

3. Vehicle and Driver Assumptions Used for Evaluation

 

The following assumptions define the evaluation scenario and do not introduce additional requirements:

 

a) Initial Conditions: 

  • Ego and Lead Vehicle travel at the same steady state speed v.
  • Initial bumper to bumper distance is d0.
  • Ego acceleration at t=0 is zero (steady-state following).

 

b) Driver Reaction:

    Perception–Reaction Time (PRT) = 0.75  seconds (trained safety driver responding to automation cues)
 

c) Lead Vehicle Braking: constant longitudinal deceleration: 
bLV = 0.65 g  = 6.37m/s2

 

d) Ego Vehicle Braking: Jerk bounded S curve braking: 

  • Peak deceleration: bmax = 8.0 m/s2
  • Ramp in jerk: J↓ = 10 m/s3
  • Ramp out jerk: J↑ = 7.5 m/s3

4. Zero-Offset Gap Construction

 

To determine the minimum required distance, a zero-offset simulation is defined:

 

5. Physics Based Minimum Distance
The physics-based minimum distance required to satisfy the all-times gap condition is:
dmin_physics⁡ (v) = MAX (Dmargin - gmin (v) , 0)

 

This term ensures that the minimum gap never falls below Dmargin = 1.5 m at any time

 

6. Human-Factors Constraint on Time Headway
Analysis shows that at highway speeds the physics-based solution alone can yield time headways as low as 0.39 seconds, which is not considered acceptable for real world drivers.
To ensure human realistic following behavior, a minimum time headway equal to the assumed driver PRT is enforced:
THW(v) ≥ PRT

This constraint is equivalent to enforcing:
dmin_PRT (v) = v⋅  PRT

fields.name: Longitudinal time-to-collision (TTC) for ado cut-ins
fields.description:
REQUIREMENT STATEMENT

During an ado CUT-IN while dlong ≥ 0m, the ego vehicle SHALL:

  1. maintain a time-to-contact (TTC) >= 2.0 seconds with a fault tolerant time interval (FTTI) >= 100 ms

  1. AND reach at least one of two possible states within tstop seconds from when ado’s BOUNDING BOX protrudes into ego’s lane by a distance >= 0.30m:

    1. satisfy the dmin requirement of HSR4 without a collision

    2. reach a speed of vego = 0 m/s without a collision

 

 

The following assumptions were made:

  1. vf = 0 m/s

  2. a0 = 0m/s2

  3. amax = -1 m/s2

  4. j0 = 0 m/s3

  5. jmax = -2.5 m/s3

  6. tlatency = 0.820 s

Definition of CUT-IN ado: any moving traffic participant (car, truck, motorcycle, bicycle, etc) that simultaneously satisfies the following conditions:

  • The ado’s BOUNDING BOX protrudes into the ego lane by a distance ≥ 0.30 meters

  • The distance between the front most point of ego’s BOUNDING BOX and the rearmost point of the ado’s BOUNDING BOX is a longitudinal distance, dlong, between -1.8 m ≤ dlong < dmin from HSR4. 

 

 

Definition of “end of CUT-IN maneuver”: The cut-in maneuver is said to be complete when the ego vehicle reaches EITHER state 2a or 2b.

 

RATIONALE

Why: Stay within safe boundaries

Keep safe lateral and longitudinal distance to cutting in ados

 

Thresholds:

TTC: During a cut-in, the ego vehicle is expected to not approach the cut-in vehicle too quickly and to retain some longitudinal space to the cut-in vehicle.  The data published in Wang, X, Yang, M, Hurwitz, D. “Analysis of cut-in behavior based on naturalistic driving data”. Accident Analysis and Prevention, 124, 2019, pp. 127-137. shows that a vast majority of cut-ins in real-world driving have a minimum TTC ≥ 2s (Figure 5).  UN Regulation 157 also contains a driver model for a cut-in scenario that defines 2 seconds as “the maximum TTC below which it was concluded that there is a danger of collision in the longitudinal direction” (see top of pg. 44).


Time tstop: The ego vehicle should not violate the dmin requirement from HSR4 for too long after a cut-in.  In the worst case, the cut-in vehicle comes to a stop with a deceleration that is less than or equal to the ego vehicle’s deceleration, meaning condition 2a can never be satisfied before reaching 2b.  Defining the violation time limit as the time it takes the ego vehicle to gently brake from its current speed permits the ego vehicle to reach condition 2b without placing too strict of a requirement on the amount of braking the ego vehicle must use during a cut-in

fields.name: Driving in-lane - Lateral distance to ado vehicles and static obstacles
fields.description:
REQUIREMENT STATEMENT

While driving in-lane, the ego vehicle SHALL keep the minimum lateral distance, dlat, between the closest point of the ego vehicle's FOOTPRINT and the FOOTPRINT of any adjacent vehicles (static or dynamic) and/or static obstacles, WHERE dlat is linearly interpolated based on ego’s current speed using the nearest data points in the table below.

RATIONALE

Why: Stay within safe boundaries  - keeping safe lateral distance to ados and other obstacles

 

Thresholds:

Distance dlat: The data originates from lateral recoverability studies performed on the TMPOC platform and indicates the “mean + 3σ”(i.e., reasonable maximum) amount of lateral deviation observed after a steering fault was injected.  Maintaining a lateral distance to other vehicles/objects that is greater than the lateral deviation value ensures that there will not be a collision even if ego suddenly begins steering towards the other vehicle/object. The values have been rounded up to the nearest tenth.

 

Time: Outliers are tolerated for a short period of time to account for sensor, perception and localization inaccuracies/uncertainties. A time period of 1 second accounts for the expected reaction time of the safety driver.

fields.name: Handling traffic lights - Distance to stop line
fields.description:
REQUIREMENT STATEMENT

When required to stop for a signal, the ego vehicle SHALL stop behind the stop line with a distance dSL≥ 0 meter measured between the front of the ego vehicle's FOOTPRINT and the stop line.

 

 

RATIONALE

Why: Stay within safe boundaries and obey traffic laws

 

Thresholds:

Distance dSL: Whenever the ego vehicle is required to stop for a traffic light, the minimum expectation is to always stop behind the stop line to prevent potentially blocking the intersection in any way.
 

 

 

 

    

EVALUATION CRITERIA

PASS criteria: 

  • dSL≥ 0 meter on a red traffic light

 

FAIL criteria:

  • dSL< 0 meter on a red traffic light

NOTES

“Required to stop” is referring to a red traffic light.

fields.name: Driving in-lane -- Steering Sway
fields.description:
REQUIREMENT TITLE

Driving in-lane - Steering sway

REQUIREMENT STATEMENT

While driving in-lane, the waveform of the ego vehicle’s lateral position in its lane over a 5 second window (2.5s before - 2.5s after) SHALL have an amplitude alat ≤ alat,MAX for cycles that have a frequency f ≥ 1/3 Hz

 

WHERE,

  • alat,MAX =  0.5 * (dΔlat,max - wego)

  • dΔlat,max = 0.8 * lane width [m]

  • wego = 2.20m

  • alat = max offset for half cycle time - average offset over 5s window

  • f = 1/(2*T)

  • T = half cycle time (from one crossing of the 5s average offset to the next)

 

RATIONALE

Why: Avoiding unreasonable driving behavior

Unreasonable swerving in lane could harm Toyota’s public appearance and put higher burden on the Safety Driver

 

Thresholds:

Amplitude alat: This requirement is addressing wide swerves from one side to the other. The threshold marks the point where the lateral displacement distance between the left and right swerve is covering more than 80% of the total lane width, assuming that the profile of the swerve is symmetric.

 

Frequency f: A minimum frequency of 1/3 (or a full cycle time of ≥ 3 seconds) is selected because of the following considerations:

  1. A lateral maneuver that violates the amplitude threshold with a cycle time >3 seconds is estimated as a more minor swerving behavior even at higher speeds

  2. When driving at lower speeds, it is estimated that a large swerve can still be done within 3 seconds

  3. Setting the minimum frequency to 1/3 ensures that the HSR is less strict than the final sway performance requirement from TMC

fields.name: Driving in-lane - Lateral distance when overtaking bicycle in bike lane
fields.description:
REQUIREMENT STATEMENT

When overtaking and passing a pedal cyclist that is positioned within a bike lane and traveling in the same direction as the ego vehicle, the ego vehicle SHALL maintain a minimum lateral gap dLGB to the bicyclist.

 

With:

California: dLGB ≥  3 foot (0.92m)

Michigan (Ann Arbor): dLGB ≥  5 foot (1.52m)

RATIONALE

Why: Stay within safe boundaries of lane, a bicyclist, and with compliance of CVC 21760 for California and for Ann Arbor compliance of Amends sec. 636 of 1949 PA 300 (MCL 257.636)

…

(c) A driver of a motor vehicle shall not overtake or pass a bicycle proceeding in the same direction on a highway at a distance of less than three feet between any part of the motor vehicle and any part of the bicycle or its operator. The driver of a motor vehicle overtaking or passing a bicycle that is proceeding in the same direction and in the same lane of travel shall, if another lane of traffic proceeding in the same direction is available, make a lane change into another available lane with due regard for safety and traffic conditions, if practicable and not prohibited by law, before overtaking or passing the bicycle.

 

(d) If the driver of a motor vehicle is unable to comply with subdivision (c), due to traffic or roadway conditions, the driver shall slow to a speed that is reasonable and prudent, and may pass only when doing so would not endanger the safety of the operator of the bicycle, taking into account the size and speed of the motor vehicle and bicycle, traffic conditions, weather, visibility, and surface and width of the highway.

 

Thresholds:

Distance dLGB: For basic in-lane driving with discernible left and right lane boundaries (lane marking or lane edge), the vehicle’s footprint is expected to never leave the lane boundaries dLB and get within 3 ft (0.92m) of the bicycle. This is represented by a threshold of 0.92m.

 

Through analysis of  the  P4A Lateral Recoverability after Steering Fault Injections the max lateral deviation for going 35 mph is 0.17m and 45 mph is 0.34m.  By maintaining a 0.92m distance this assures that Ego will not come into contact with a cyclist if a lateral steering request occurs just below the SMABX thresholds.

fields.name: 9a Longitudinal distance to rear ado vehicles in target lane
fields.description:
While changing lanes or merging, the ego vehicle SHALL have a longitudinal distance > dmin between the closest point of the ego vehicle's FOOTPRINT and the ado vehicle behind in the target  lane at the moment ego starts crossing the lane boundary.

 

 

 

WHERE

AV : Autonomous Vehicle (ego vehicle)

SFV :  Side Follow Vehicle in target lane

 

The following assumptions were made:

  1. Reaction time of SFV driver from the moment AV begins crossing the lane boundary taken from UN-R79.

  1. tb = 0.4 sec

  1. Remaining time gap between SFV and AV as specified in UN-R79.

    1. tGap = 1 sec

  2. Comfortable deceleration of SFV as specified in UN-R79.

    1. aSFV = -3 m/s2

  3. Magic constant that defines the separation when AV is traveling faster than SFV

    1. Dmargin = max(5.0, Ado THW: 1 sec)

RATIONALE

A rear vehicle in the target lane has the potential to collide when driving at higher speed than ego. This requirement specifies the minimum distance that limits the deceleration of the rear vehicle to a threshold

fields.name: Lane change - Lane change operation to incorrect lane
fields.description:
REQUIREMENT STATEMENT

The ego vehicle SHALL not initiate a lane change if any of the following conditions are met:

  1. The target lane is not a drivable lane (i.e., the lane change would take the ego vehicle off of the road).

  2. The ego vehicle would have to change lanes in an intersection to reach the target lane.

  3. The ego vehicle would have to cross a double, solid yellow line to reach the target lane.

  4. The ego vehicle would have to cross a single, solid yellow line to reach the target lane.

  5. The ego vehicle would have to cross the solid portion of a double yellow line with one solid line and one broken line first to reach the target lane unless the target lane is a shared left turn lane that the ego vehicle must use to turn left.

  6. The ego vehicle would have to cross a double, solid white line to reach the target lane.

  7. The ego vehicle would have to cross a single, solid white line to reach the target lane.*

RATIONALE

Why: Avoid lane change to non-drivable lanes, wrong direction traffic

Keeping ego in drivable lane
 

NOTES:

 

*Statement (7) in the REQUIREMENT STATEMENT section should not cause a failure of this HSR if there is a condition that makes the lane change necessary (e.g., there is a hazard in the lane ahead).

fields.name: Turn signal operation
fields.description:
REQUIREMENT STATEMENT

Prior to turning a vehicle from a direct course, the ego vehicle SHALL activate, and continuously use, its turn signal corresponding to the intended direction of motion for: 

  1. A distance d ≥ 100 feet (30.48 meters) prior to crossing the lane boundary of the target lane, or entering the branch that will take the vehicle off the direct course.

RATIONALE

Why: Avoid unreasonable driving behavior and obey traffic laws. CVC 22017 states that “no person shall turn a vehicle from a direct course or move right or left upon a roadway until such movement can be made with reasonable safety and then only after giving an appropriate signal in the manner provided.”

 

Thresholds:

Distance d: Reusing the former TRI requirement Chauf-SYSRQ-3 which ensures that turn signal operation is in compliance with CVC 22108.  This code states that “Any signal of intention to turn right or left shall be given continuously during the last 100 feet traveled by the vehicle before turning.”

fields.name: HSR4a: Longitudinal time-to-collision (TTC) for ado cut-ins
fields.description:
EVALUATION CRITERIA

PASS criteria: 

  • EITHER

    • TTC ≥ 2.0 seconds

    • TTC < 2.0 seconds for ≤ 100 milliseconds

  • EITHER

    • vego = 0 m/s within tstop without collision

    • d ≥ dmin within tstop without collision

FAIL criteria:

  • Ego collides with ado cut-in OR

  • TTC < 2.0 seconds for > 100 milliseconds OR

  • BOTH of the following conditions are true:

    • vego > 0 m/s after tstop 

    • d < dmin after tstop

NOTES

  • During a CUT-IN, it is permissible for ego to temporarily violate the HSR4 dmin requirement.

  • For overlapped cut-ins (where dlong is initially < 0m), HSR5 applies until dlong ≥ 0m (cut-in ado is ahead of ego). Once dlong ≥ 0m, the criteria specified here in HSR4a applies.

 

 

DESCRIPTION

Verifying that ego is keeping a minimum longitudinal time-to-collision (TTC) for ado cut-ins:

  • In-lane driving only

  • On straight road sections

  • Average lane width of GG’24 route (3.6 meter)

fields.name: HSR 5: Driving in-lane - Lateral distance to ado vehicles and static obstacles
fields.description:
EVALUATION CRITERIA

PASS criteria:

  • lateral distance > dlat

  • lateral distance ≤ dlat for ≤ 1 second

FAIL criteria:

  • lateral distance ≤ dlat for > 1 second

 

NOTES

  • The data points for dlat come from the following sources:

    • TMPOC Lateral Recoverability with urban limits

  • “Adjacent” implies that there is a > 0% longitudinal overlap between the ego vehicle and the ado vehicle / object.

 

DESCRIPTION

Verifying that ego is keeping a minimum lateral distance to other vehicles/obstacles while driving in-lane:

  • In-lane driving only

  • Lane width ≥ the minimum allowable lane width based on TMPOC Lateral Recoverability with urban limits

  • Scenarios with sufficient available lateral space* to pass both with and without the need to slow down

    • *Available lateral space: to be measured between the static vehicle/obstacle and the lane boundary 

  • NOTE: TMPOC footprint width = 2.20 meter (including mirrors)

fields.name: HSR7: Driving in-lane - Steering sway
fields.description:
EVALUATION CRITERIA

  

PASS criteria: 

  • alat ≤ alat,MAX OR

  • (alat > alat,MAX AND f < 1/3 Hz)

FAIL criteria:

  • alat > alat,MAX AND f ≥ 1/3 Hz

 

 

NOTES

  • The requirement is only addressing basic in-lane driving with no ados or obstacles ahead.

  • The requirement only applies when ego is driving on lanes that are ≥ 10ft (3.048m) wide.

    • 10 ft lanes are the typical minimum lane width for urban areas as recommended by the American Association of State Highway and Transportation Officials (AASHTO) in “A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets” (see pg. 8 of this report for a reference)

    • The design guide of the National Association of City Transportation Officials (NACTO) recommends a standard lane width of 10 ft in urban areas

    • At a lane width of 9 ft, ego is wider than dΔlat,max, meaning the maximum amplitude is negative (requirement is impossible to achieve). In these cases, this requirement should be disregarded and HSR1a and HSR1b should be followed.

 

 

  

DESCRIPTION

Verifying that is ego is not swerving between lane boundaries:

  • Same test scenarios as HSR1a

  • Basic in-lane driving only

  • No other agents 

  • Minimum radius of curved road to be based on minimum radius specified in ODD and available at closed course test tracks

  • Clear lane boundaries

  • Lane width of ≥ 10ft (3.048m)

fields.name: HSR8: Driving in-lane - Lateral distance when overtaking bicycle in bike lane
fields.description:
EVALUATION CRITERIA

 

 

PASS criteria:

 

  • Distance to bicycle is > dLGB

FAIL criteria:

  • Distance to bicycle is < dLGB

 

 

NOTES

California:

  • The average lane width of Foothill Loop is 3.6m and the side mirror to side mirror width of the P4a vehicle is 2.19 meters.  Staying in the center of the lane puts the distance from the right lane boundary (and the bike lane) at 0.705m.  This is less than the 0.92m threshold required.  Therefore Ego will need to nudge to the left in order to maintain 0.92m separation.

  

 

 

 

 

  • If Ego nudges to the left to maintain 0.92m separation this leaves a 0.49m gap to the left lane boundary and Ego should stay within its lane corridor.

 

 

 

  • If the lateral space between the bicycle and right lane boundary is ≥0.215m then Ego does not need to nudge

 

EVALUATION DESCRIPTION:

 

Verifying basic stay in-lane driving on straight with clear discernible lane boundaries and overtaking a bicycle traveling in the same direction:

  • Basic in-lane driving only

  • Clear lane boundaries

  • Speed limit 25 mph (due to test track limitations)

  • Average lane width of GG’24 route (3.6 meter)

  • Average bike lane width 5ft  (1.524m)

One bicyclist outside of egos lane with: 

  1. Available lateral space from right lane boundary = 0 - 0.2 meter (left position)

  2. Available lateral space from right lane boundary = 0.4 - 0.6* meter (center position)

*This is meant to position the bicycle in the middle of a 5ft (1.524m) bike lane with a center at 0.762m.  The test dummy has a shoulder width of 0.5m.  Therefore the lateral space from the right lane boundary to the left side of the dummy is calculated to be 0.762m - (0.5m/2) = 0.512m. Allowing ~0.1m variance in positioning results in a range of 0.4 - 0.6m

fields.name: HSR9c: Turn signal operation
fields.description:
EVALUATION CRITERIA

 

PASS criteria: 

  • The vehicle’s turn signal is activated more than or equal to 100 feet before the vehicle starts to cross the lane line, AND the vehicle’s turn signal is active until the vehicle has fully centered itself in the target lane. 

FAIL criteria:

  • The vehicle’s turn signal is activated less than 100 feet before the vehicle starts to cross the lane line, OR the vehicle’s turn signal is deactivated prior to the vehicle fully centering itself in the target lane.

 

PASS Criteria

  • The vehicle’s turn signal is activated more than or equal to 100 feet before the vehicle enters a branch, AND the vehicle’s turn signal is active until the vehicle has fully taken the branch. 

 

FAIL Criteria

  • The vehicle’s turn signal is activated less than 100 feet before the vehicle enters a branch, OR the vehicle’s turn signal is deactivated before the vehicle has fully taken the branch.

 

PASS Criteria 

  • The vehicle’s turn signal is activated more than or equal to 100 feet before the vehicle enters a merge, AND the vehicle’s turn signal is active until the vehicle is fully centered in the lane of the road post merging.  

 

FAIL Criteria 

  • The vehicle’s turn signal is activated less than 100 feet before the vehicle enters a merge, OR the vehicle’s turn signal is deactivated before the vehicle is fully centered in the lane of the road post merging.


 

 

EVALUATION DESCRIPTION:

 

Verifying that ego signals for a minimum distance before a lane change:

  • On straight road section

  • No other agents

 

 

SCENARIO SKETCH

 

Straight road lane change

fields.name: SWRD-BC-LP_ProSt_010_SP_2
fields.description:
Objective:
Ensure LC proposal is withdrawn whenever at least one of the defined withdrawal conditions is met.

 

Scenario 1 — Exited Lane Change Assist Section

 

  1. Check VehicleExitedLCSection = true.
  2. Withdrawal condition met → set LCProposalActive = false.
  3. Expected Output: Proposal withdrawn.

Scenario 2 — Approval Timeout

 

  1. Check LCApprovalTimeoutElapsed = true.
  2. Withdrawal condition met → set LCProposalActive = false.
  3. Expected Output: Proposal withdrawn.

 

Scenario 3 — Driver Rejected Proposal

 

  1. Check DriverRejectedLCProposal = true.
  2. Withdrawal condition met → set LCProposalActive = false.
  3. Expected Output: Proposal withdrawn.

Scenario 4 — Suppression Condition Met

  1. Check LCStandbySuppressionConditionsMet = true.
  2. Withdrawal condition met → set LCProposalActive = false.
  3. Expected Output: Proposal withdrawn.

Scenario 5 — None of the Conditions Met

 

  1. None of the withdrawal conditions true.
  2. Keep LC proposal active → LCProposalActive = true.
  3. Expected Output: Proposal remains active.

fields.name: User Confirmed Lane Change
fields.description:
The Woven vehicle shall support User Confirmed Lane Change (UCLC).

 

The Woven system shall request the driver to perform a LC when system has determined that a lane change is necessary to reach a destination, avoid road debris, or if a Lane Change would make sense in order to perform an overtake maneuver.

fields.name: User Initiated Lane Change
fields.description:
The Woven System shall support User Initiated Lane Change. 

 

The Woven System shall attempt to make a lane change if the driver requests a Lane Change via the turn indicator.

fields.name: Suppression for Underspeed
fields.description:
The Lane Change feature shall be suppressed if the ego vehicle and the ado in the target lane is under the speed threshold as defined by HSR 9A. 

 

 

Rationalle:

We are limited by the vehicle dynamics and sensor capabilities of our vehicle. We need to ensure that if we move into an adjacent lane, the ado vehicle doesn't need to brake unnecessarily.

fields.name: Suppression for request to invalid lane
Abort Lane Change on Hazard Detection
fields.description: The system shall support lane change abort when an approaching vehicle in the target or adjacent lane is detected during the time from start to end of crossing the lane marker.
fields.text1:
The goal is to prevent collisions and unsafe merges by immediately halting an in‑progress lane change when a hazardous, approaching vehicle is detected in the target or adjacent lane, maintaining predictable vehicle behavior and protecting passenger comfort, stability, and safety.

Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_692#slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_692

 

Aborting a lane change maneuver means stopping or reversing an ongoing lane change in a controlled and safe manner when a hazard or unexpected condition is detected, making it unsafe to continue the maneuver.

fields.name: Allow automatic or manual trigger for Lane Change Abort
fields.description: The system shall allow lane change abort to be initiated automatically upon detection of an approaching vehicle or manually by the driver using the turn signal when ego is crossing the lane marker.
fields.text1:
The goal is to ensure the system can promptly terminate an unsafe lane change when a hazard is detected, either automatically or through driver intervention, to prevent collisions and maintain predictable, safe vehicle behavior.

Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_692#slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_692

fields.name: Supress Lane Change: Front Slower Vehicle in Target Lane
fields.description:
Given that the target vehicle is in front of the ego vehicle AND it's slower than the ego, the system shall suppress lane change availability when the distance between bumpers is less than:
dsuppress = (Relative speed2)/(2*1.96 m/s2) + (Ego speed + Relative speed)*0.2 s.
fields.text1:
The goal is to prevent lane change when the vehicle ahead is slower and the available gap is below the computed safety threshold, reducing collision risk and ensuring safe maneuvering.

Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g33230f3e303_0_0#slide=id.g33230f3e303_0_0

fields.name: Suppress Lane Change: Front Faster Vehicle in Target Lane
fields.description:
Given that the target vehicle is in front of the ego vehicle AND it's faster than the ego, the system shall suppress lane change availability when the distance between bumpers is less than:

dsuppress = MAX(-Relative speed*2.1 s + Ego speed*0.2 s, -Relative speed*1.0 s)
fields.text1:
The goal is to block lane change when the vehicle ahead is faster and the gap is insufficient, avoiding unsafe merges into rapidly closing traffic.

Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g33230f3e303_0_0#slide=id.g33230f3e303_0_0

fields.name: Allow Lane Change: Front Slower Vehicle in Target Lane
fields.description:
Given that the target vehicle is in front of the ego vehicle AND it's slower than the ego, the system shall allow lane change when the distance between bumpers is greater than:
dallow = (Relative speed2)/(2*0.98 m/s2) + (Ego speed + Relative speed)*0.6 s
fields.text1:
The goal is to permit lane change only when the target vehicle ahead is slower and the gap exceeds the calculated safety margin, ensuring predictable and safe lane change, and reducing collision risk.

 

Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g33230f3e303_0_0#slide=id.g33230f3e303_0_0

fields.name: Allow Lane Change: Front Faster Vehicle in Target Lane
fields.description:
Given that the target vehicle is in front of the ego vehicle AND it's faster than the ego, the system shall allow lane change when the distance between bumpers is greater than:

dallow = MAX(-Relative speed*2.1 s + Ego speed*0.6 s, -Relative speed*1.0 s).
fields.text1:
The goal is to ensure lane change is only allowed when sufficient margin exists, reducing collision risk, and maintaining safety.

 

Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g33230f3e303_0_0#slide=id.g33230f3e303_0_0

fields.name: Suppress Lane Change: Slower Vehicle Behind in Target Lane
fields.description:
Given that the target vehicle is behind the ego vehicle AND it's slower than the ego, the system shall suppress lane change availability when the distance between bumpers is less than:
dsuppress = MIN(-Relative speed*2.1 s - Target speed*0.2 s, -Relative speed*1.0 s) - ego length.
fields.text1:
The goal is to prevent lane change when the vehicle in the target lane is behind and slower, but the distance between both vehicles' bumpers is below the minimum safe distance, reducing rear-end collision risk.
 

Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g33230f3e303_0_0#slide=id.g33230f3e303_0_0

fields.name: Suppress Lane Change: Faster Vehicle Behind in Target Lane
fields.description:
Given that the target vehicle is behind the ego vehicle AND it's faster than the ego, the system shall suppress lane change availability when the distance between bumpers is less than:
dsuppress = -(Relative speed2)/(2*1.47 m/s2) - Ego speed*0.2 s - ego length
fields.text1:
The goal is to prevent lane change when the vehicle in the target lane is behind and faster than the ego vehicle, and the distance between bumpers is less than the safe distance, avoiding cut-in scenarios that force abrupt braking behind ego vehicle, and reducing rear-end collision risk.

Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g33230f3e303_0_0#slide=id.g33230f3e303_0_0

fields.name: Allow Lane Change: Slower Vehicle Behind in Target Lane
fields.description:
Given that the target vehicle is behind the ego vehicle AND it's slower than the ego, the system shall allow lane change when the distance between bumpers is greater than:
dallow = MIN(-Relative speed*2.1 s - Target speed*0.6 s, -Relative speed*1.0 s) - ego length
fields.text1:
When the vehicle in the target lane is behind and slower than the ego vehicle, the goal is to ensure that lane change is only allowed when the distance between bumpers exceeds the safety margin, ensuring safe distance after the maneuver, and reducing collision risk.

 

Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g33230f3e303_0_0#slide=id.g33230f3e303_0_0

fields.name: Allow Lance Change: Faster Vehicle Behind in Target Lane
fields.description:
Given that the target vehicle is behind the ego vehicle AND it's faster than the ego, the system shall allow lane change when the distance between bumpers is greater than:
dallow = -(Relative speed2)/(2*1.47 m/s2) - Ego speed*0.6 s - ego length
fields.text1:
When the vehicle in the target lane is behind and it's faster than the ego vehicle, the goal is to ensure that the lane change is only allowed when sufficient distance between both vehicles' bumpers, preventing unsafe closing speeds, maintaining maneuver safety, and reducing collision risk.

 

Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g33230f3e303_0_0#slide=id.g33230f3e303_0_0

fields.name: Standby Monitoring Between Suppress and Allow Thresholds
fields.description: Given that the distance between the ego vehicle and the target vehicle is greater than dsuppress but less than dallow, the system shall continuously monitor the distance and maintain lane change availability in a standby state until the distance becomes ≤ dsuppress to supress or ≥ dallow to allow the lane change.
fields.text1:
The goal is to ensure safe and predictable lane change decision-making by avoiding premature acceptance or rejection when distance is in the intermediate range.

Sources:

https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_444#slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_444


https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g33230f3e303_0_0#slide=id.g33230f3e303_0_0

fields.name: Suppress Lane Change Availability After Standby Timeout
fields.description: Given that the distance between the ego vehicle and the target vehicle remains greater than dsuppress but less than dallow for more than 3.0 seconds, the system shall suppress the lane change availability.
fields.text1:
The goal is to prevent indefinite standby state and ensures timely decision-making to maintain safety and predictability for lane change availability.

 

Sources:

https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_444#slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_444


https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g33230f3e303_0_0#slide=id.g33230f3e303_0_0

fields.name: Trigger Lane Change Before Deceleration When Closing on Slower Leading Vehicle
fields.description:
Given that lane change is allowed and the ego vehicle is closing on a slower vehicle ahead in the current lane, the system shall trigger the lane change before initiating deceleration, provided the distance to the leading vehicle is greater than TBD meters.

 

Note: the distance needs to be defined. Slide 66 only mentions "at distance TBD)
fields.text1:
The goal is to maintain maneuver efficiency and avoid unnecessary braking when a safe lane change is possible, ensuring smooth traffic flow and vehicle stability.

Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_618#slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_618

fields.name: Initiation Tirgger
fields.description:
The Woven System shall recognize a user-initiated lane change request when the driver partially presses or lifts the turn indicator stalk for greater than 0.5 seconds. 

 

Rationale: 

The turn indicator has five states. 

  • Neutral 
  • Momentary Left
  • Latched Left
  • Momentary Right 
  • Latched Right

The automatic lane change system will only respond to momentary presses of the turn indicator stalk.

fields.name: Direction of the turn indicator Salk
fields.description: The Lane Change direction shall match the direction of the turn indicator stalk operation.

fields.name: Searching For Gap
fields.description:
For User Initiated Lane Change, the woven system shall look for a gap to maneuver the ego vehicle into the target lane for a maximum of 10 seconds prior to aborting the lane change gap search. 

 

For User Confirmed Lane change  the woven system shall look for a gap to maneuver the ego vehicle into the target lane for a maximum of 30 seconds prior to aborting the lane change gap search.

fields.name: Spatial Clearance for Gap
fields.description:
The minimum front clearance from the front bumper of the ego vehicle to the rear bumper of the forward ado vehicle shall be x meters upon completion of the maneuver. 

 

The minimum rear clearance from the rear bumper of the ego vehicle to the rear bumper of the forward ado vehicle shall be y meters upon immediate completion of the maneuver.

fields.name: Adjusting Speed to find LC gap
fields.description:
The woven system shall adjust the speed of the ego vehicle in order to more quickly maneuver into the target gap for the Lane Change.

 

Rationalle: 

 

SYRD: GID-3607859

fields.name: Turn Signal Operation
fields.description:
Prior to turning a vehicle from a direct course, the ego vehicle SHALL activate, and continuously use, its turn signal corresponding to the intended direction of motion for a distance d ≥ 100 feet (30.48 meters) OR for a time of 3 seconds

  1. Prior to crossing the lane boundary of the target lane, or

  2. entering the branch that will take the vehicle off the direct course.

Rationalle: 
UN vehicle regulations is where the 3 second threshold is: https://unece.org/sites/default/files/2025-03/R171e.pdf

California vehicle regulations: https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=VEH&sectionNum=22108

 

Note: there is some ambiguity with phrasing in the regulation if the moment that measurement begins is from when the vehicle veers from direct course or if it's from when the vehicle crosses the lane boundary.

fields.name: Lateral Acceleration Range Limit
fields.description: The system shall maintain lateral acceleration within 0.3 - 0.8 m/s² during the lane change maneuver.
fields.text1:
The goal is to ensure passenger comfort and vehicle stability while avoiding excessive lateral forces.

The design limits used in this requirement are listed in the slide (link below), and are within the values set by UN R-79 §5.6.4.4 and UN R-157 § 5.2.6.6.1.

Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g2800b7ab536_0_551#slide=id.g2800b7ab536_0_551

fields.name: Lateral Jerk Limit
fields.description: The system shall ensure lateral jerk does not exceed 1.0 m/s³ during the maneuver.
fields.text1:
The goal is to limit sudden changes in lateral acceleration, improving comfort and reducing risk of loss of control.

Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g2800b7ab536_0_551#slide=id.g2800b7ab536_0_551

fields.name: Steering Smoothness
fields.description: Max steering wheel rate shall not exceed x degrees/ second during maneuver

fields.name: Maximum Lateral Velocity during lane change trajectory
fields.description: The maximum lateral velocity shall occur between 35% and 45% of the lane change trajectory, with the total lane change trajectory distance being measured from the moment the lane change starts to the moment the lane change maneuver ends.
fields.text1:
The goal is to ensure a smooth and predictable lateral motion profile, avoiding aggressive or delayed maneuvers.

Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g2800b7ab536_0_551#slide=id.g2800b7ab536_0_551

fields.name: Minimum Time Before Starting Lane Crossing
fields.description: The maneuver shall take at least 1.5 seconds the moment the lane change maneuver starts to the point where the vehicle starts to cross into the target lane.
fields.text1:
Provides sufficient time for safe maneuver execution without abrupt lateral movements. This is the minimum time the system is expected to take between starting the maneuver and starting crossing the actual lane boundary.
​​​​​​
Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g2800b7ab536_0_551#slide=id.g2800b7ab536_0_551

fields.name: Limit Overshoot Once Lane Change Maneuver is Complete
fields.description: The system shall limit overshoot from the center of the target lane to ≤ 0.2 m once the lane change maneuver has been completed and the vehicle reached a steady state in the target lane.
fields.text1:
Ensures accurate lane positioning and prevents oscillations or instability post-maneuver.

Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g2800b7ab536_0_551#slide=id.g2800b7ab536_0_551

fields.name: Ensure Continuous Lane Change Movement
fields.description: Given that a lane change maneuver is in progress (measure from lateral velocity ≥ 0.2 m/s until lane change completion), the system shall ensure that the maneuver is completed in one single continuous movement, with no second steering input detected during the maneuver.
fields.text1:
Avoids unnatural or unsafe steering patterns that could confuse other road users or reduce comfort.

Sources:
https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g2800b7ab536_0_551#slide=id.g2800b7ab536_0_551
UN-R79 § 5.6.4.6.4

fields.name: Timing to Initiate Lane Change
fields.description: The system shall initiate lateral movement with a lateral velocity relative to the lane marking ≥ 0.2 m/s within 2.2–3.0 seconds after a lane change is requested by the driver or initiated by the system.
fields.text1:
The goal is to ensure that the lane change maneuver does not take long to start once it is requested by the driver or triggered by the system.

Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g2800b7ab536_0_551#slide=id.g2800b7ab536_0_551

fields.name: Timing to Start Lane Boundary Crossing
fields.description: The system shall ensure the ego vehicle starts crossing the lane marking within 1.0-2.0 s after the lateral movement begins.
fields.text1:
The goal is to ensure smooth progression from lateral movement to lane crossing, once the lane change maneuver has started.

Sources:
https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g2800b7ab536_0_551#slide=id.g2800b7ab536_0_551
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1F3gbraGto4LrvRpMXyKP2D7bEKFBkkWEDQEH6d7XF4s/

 

"Start crossing the lane line" is defined as the first instant at which any point on the ego vehicle’s footprint intercepts or overlaps the lane boundary marking. This occurs when the minimum lateral distance between the ego vehicle’s footprint and the lane line transitions from a positive value to zero or negative.

Vehicle footprint refers to the ground‑projected area of the vehicle’s body, measured by its physical length and width on the road surface, excluding mirrors and other protruding elements.

fields.name: Time Limit to Complete Lane Change
fields.description: The system shall ensure the ego vehicle completely crosses into the target lane within 2.25-3.25 s after starting to cross the lane marking.
fields.text1:
The goal is to ensure that the lane change maneuver is completed within a safe and predictable time window.

Sources:
https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g2800b7ab536_0_551#slide=id.g2800b7ab536_0_551
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1F3gbraGto4LrvRpMXyKP2D7bEKFBkkWEDQEH6d7XF4s/

 

"Completely crosses into the target lane" is defined as the first instant at which the entire footprint of the ego vehicle lies within the boundaries of the target lane, with no part of the vehicle’s footprint overlapping or intersecting the original lane’s boundary line.

Vehicle footprint refers to the ground‑projected area of the vehicle’s body, measured by its physical length and width on the road surface, excluding mirrors and other protruding elements.

fields.name: Blinker Activation and Hold Duration
fields.description: The system shall hold the blinker for at least 0.5 seconds before initiating lateral movement and maintain it until the maneuver is completed.
fields.text1:
Provides clear signaling to surrounding traffic that a lane change maneuver is going to start or it is in progress, reducing risk of collision with other vehicles.
Slide 18 on GG24 (link below) indicates 0.5 seconds, but this time seems too short. UN R-79 does not mention any value.

Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g2800b7ab536_0_551#slide=id.g2800b7ab536_0_551

fields.name: Minimum Turn‑Signal Waiting Time Before Lane Change
fields.description: Given that the blinker stalk has been activated, the system shall start the lane change maneuver no earlier than 1.0 second after blinker activation for driver‑initiated lane changes, and no earlier than 3.0 seconds after blinker activation for system‑initiated lane changes.
fields.text1:
The goal is to ensure that surrounding road users receive clear advance indication of lane change intent and that the maneuver begins in a predictable and safe manner by enforcing a minimum waiting period between turn‑signal activation and lateral movement.
 

Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g2800b7ab536_0_551#slide=id.g2800b7ab536_0_551

fields.name: Longitudinal Acceleration Limits
fields.description: The system shall maintain longitudinal acceleration within the range of −2.9 m/s² to +1.4 m/s² during the lane change maneuver.
fields.text1:
The goal is to maintain longitudinal acceleration within defined limits, preventing abrupt acceleration or deceleration that could compromise vehicle stability, passenger comfort, and surrounding traffic safety.

Sources:

https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_544#slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_544

https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_470#slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_470

fields.name: Longitudinal Jerk Limits
fields.description: The system shall maintain longitudinal jerk within the range of −1.6 m/s³ to +1.4 m/s³ during the lane change maneuver.
fields.text1:
The goal is to keep longitudinal jerk within defined limits to prevent sudden speed changes that could compromise passenger comfort, vehicle stability, and overall safety.

Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_544#slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_544

fields.name: Lateral Jerk Limits During Abort
fields.description: During lane change abort, the system shall limit lateral jerk to ≤ 3.0 m/s³.
fields.text1:
The goal is to restrict lateral jerk during an abort maneuver to minimize sudden lateral movements, enhancing vehicle stability, maintaining predictable handling, and improving passenger comfort.

 

Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_692#slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_692

fields.name: Minimum TTC at 0% Overlap During Lane Change Maneuver
fields.description: The system shall maintain a minimum Time-to-Collision (TTC) of ≥ 4.5 s at 0% overlap during the maneuver.
fields.text1:
The goal is to ensure safe distance from preceding vehicle during lane change, to reduce risk of rear-end collisions.

Sources: 
https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_544#slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_544

Overlap is defined as illustrated below and presented at: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g33778702c08_3_3#slide=id.g33778702c08_3_3

fields.name: Delay New Lane Change Trigger after Rejection
fields.description: Given that a lane change request was rejected due to insufficient calculated safe distance, the system shall not accept a new lane change trigger for at least TBD seconds after the rejection, or until the availability condition exceeds the allowed threshold by a defined margin.
fields.text1:
The goal is to avoid oscillating availability status of the lane change maneuver that could cause unpredictable behavior.

Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_340#slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_340
 

Slide 55 mentions "no hunting of L/C availability" and Mahesh's comment mentions hysteresis: "This means hysteresis requirement of 'do not accept LC after rejecting LC' within <req_time> seconds."
<req_time> is still to be defined. Link to the comment: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?disco=AAABdqyOHG4

fields.name: Suppress Lane Change Availability when THW is too low
fields.description: Given that the calculated Time Headway (THW) is less than 0.2 s, the system shall suppress lane change availability.
fields.text1:
The goal is to provide a safety margin based on speed and distance, reducing collision risk.

 

Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_340#slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_340

fields.name: Prevent Oscillation of Lane Change Availability Using Hysteresis Logic
fields.description: Given that lane change availability conditions fluctuate near threshold values, the system shall prevent hunting by implementing hysteresis logic.
fields.text1:
The goal is to avoid oscillating availability of lane change maneuver that could lead to unpredictable behavior.

Threshold values need to be defined.

 

Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_340#slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_340

fields.name: Suppress Lane Change Availability at 50% Overlap
fields.description: Given that the target vehicle is in front of the ego vehicle, the system shall suppress lane change availability when THW between ego and target is less than 1.0 second at the moment when lateral overlap ratio reaches 50%.
fields.text1:
The goal is to prevent unsafe lane change maneuver when vehicle overlapping occurs.

Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_340#slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_340
​​​​​​​
Overlap is defined as illustrated below and presented at: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g33778702c08_3_3#slide=id.g33778702c08_3_3

fields.name: Suppress Lane Change Availability at Steering Start
fields.description: Given that the target vehicle is in front of the ego vehicle, the system shall suppress lane change availability when the longitudinal distance between bumpers is less than 4.50 m at the moment when the ego vehicle starts to steer (lateral velocity ≥ 0.2 m/s).
fields.text1:
The goal is to prevent unsafe lane change maneuver when targe vehicle is too close and steering starts.

 

Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_340#slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_340

The distance = 4.5m is defined in https://docs.google.com/document/d/1XhPf37NYXy7GJu0keRSaVfNJzChBrT0ePFXVh7UvWp4/

fields.name: Distance Measurement Calculation Precision
fields.description:
The system shall calculate and apply distance measurement with a precision tolerance of ±1 m to determine Lane Change availability thresholds.

(Note: 1.0 m of precision seems to be too high and is going to be confirmed)
fields.text1:
The goal is to ensure accurate evaluation of the Lane Change availability based on distance and reducing decision error.

 

Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_444#slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_444

fields.name: Safe Lane Return After Abort
fields.description: Given that a lane change abort is triggered, the system shall return the ego vehicle to its original lane and maintain a minimum lateral distance of at least 0.3 m from the adjacent lane marking that was intended to be crossed.
fields.text1:
The goal is to maintain a controlled return to the original lane with a defined clearance from the adjacent lane marking, ensuring predictable vehicle positioning, minimizing lateral collision risk, and supporting overall maneuver safety.

 

Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_692#slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_692

fields.name: Safe Lane Change Abort Across ODD Conditions
fields.description: The system shall perform lane change abort within the operational design domain (ODD), including curved road segments, while meeting lateral jerk and stability requirements.
fields.text1:
The goal is to ensure that lane change abort functionality operates safely across all conditions within the operational design domain (ODD), including curved roads, by maintaining lateral jerk and stability limits. This prevents abrupt maneuvers that could compromise vehicle control, passenger comfort, or and safety of surrounding vehicles.

Source: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14XbKTJ_Adt6kS8y3Slhlz9qy0JAUAJN2jycEJKxcRrA/edit?slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_692#slide=id.g32d9f0093d7_5_692

fields.name: Lane Change Complete
fields.description:
Once the lane change has been completed, the HMI system shall: 

  • Turn off the turn indicator
  • Display that the lane change has been complete.

 

Rationalle: 

SYRD GID-121343

fields.name: Turn Signal Throughout Maneuver
fields.description: The system shall ensure the turn signal remains active during the entire lane change maneuver in accordance with regional traffic laws.

fields.name: Speed Limit Thresholds-- No ADO within detection boundary
fields.description:
If there is no ado vehicle detected behind the ego vehicle, the ego vehicle shall initiate a lane change maneuver only when the following condition is satisfied:

The ego vehicle is assumed that the approaching vehicle is at the outer edge of the perception boundary, travelling at a speed equal to 10% above the maximum permissible speed for the road segment. The sensor detection boundary is defined as 90 meters from the side. 

  • Vego: Ego vehicle speed in meters per second (m/s).

  • Vado: Speed of approaching vehicle in the target path, assumed to be 10% greater than the speed limit of the road, in accordance with UN-R171; Va = 1.1 × SpeedLimit.

  • R: Furthest rear-facing sensor detection range in metres (m)

  • Amax = reasonable braking deceleration, assumed to be 3m/s2 according to UN regulations.​​​​​​
fields.text1:
Formula derivation: 

UN R-171 accepted formula uses the braking-distance model D = v^2 / 2*a.

The accepted UN formula is to assume that ego is traveling at the speed limit prior to making a lane change. This doesn’t make sense for our urban applications so we’ll bound ourselves further setting V = the delta between our 110% over speed limit and our ego speed. 

Source

fields.name: Vehicle Following Function
fields.description: Vehicle Following(VF) refers to the function that runs the ego at a vehicle speed set by the driver, follows a vehicle while maintaining a distance from the vehicle ahead, and stops in front of the vehicle.

fields.name: Emergency Maneuver Function
fields.description: Emergency Maneuver(EM) refers to a function that avoids collision or reduces damage by decelerating the ego rapidly when there is a possibility of collision with the vehicle ahead.

fields.name: Concept - Comfort
fields.description: The system shall aim for "comfortable acceleration and deceleration performance" that does not cause accidents or signs of accidents, similar to an experienced driver.

fields.name: Concept-Safety
fields.description: The system shall "avoid collision with the vehicle ahead or mitigate damage while the system is in operation" by rapidly decelerating when the system determines there is a high possibility of a collision due to a sudden change in the driving environment.

fields.name: Concept - Driver Tolerance
fields.description: The system shall "not tolerate unacceptable and unnecessary operation by the driver" to ensure system operation does not make the vehicle unsafe or induce new accidents.

fields.name: Peak Acceleration From 0 kph to 60 kph
fields.description: When accelerating from 0 mph to 60 mph, the peak acceleration shall be between 0.96 mps2 and 1.44 mps2.

fields.name: Peak Jerk From 0kph to 60 kph
fields.description: When accelerating from 0kph to 60kph, the peak jerk shall be between 0.69mps3 and 1.04mps3.
