fields.name: Propose fastest‑lane‑exit lane change
fields.description:
The Dynamic Lane Change function shall propose a fastest‑lane‑exit lane change when ALL of the following conditions are true:

  • the ego vehicle is driving in the fastest lane,
  • the ego vehicle has continuously remained in that lane for at least the configured distance or time,
  • automated driving has been active for at least the configured activation‑support time,
  • the ego vehicle is not performing an overtaking maneuver,
  • the forward‑direction blinker is off, AND
  • a target‑lane space that meets the lane‑change acceptance thresholds is available.
fields.rationale$589: The goal is to ensures that a fastest‑lane‑exit proposal is generated only when the ego vehicle has remained in the fastest lane beyond the permitted duration or distance, and when conditions support a safe and lawful return to a slower lane.

fields.name: Withdraw Fastest‑Lane‑Exit Lane Change Proposal
fields.description:
The Dynamic Lane Change function shall withdraw the fastest‑lane‑exit lane‑change proposal when ANY of the following conditions become true:

  • lane‑change assistance is unavailable in the current road section,
  • the driver rejects the proposal,
  • the ego vehicle is no longer in the fastest lane,
  • the surrounding environment no longer supports returning to the original lane, OR
  • performing the lane change would prevent reaching the destination.
fields.rationale$589: Withdrawal is required when driver intent, environmental conditions, or operational constraints invalidate the original justification for performing the fastest‑lane‑exit lane change.

fields.name: Record Reason for Withdrawal of Fastest‑Lane‑Exit Lane Change Proposal
fields.description: The Dynamic Lane Change function shall record the applicable withdrawal reason whenever a fastest‑lane‑exit lane‑change proposal is withdrawn.
fields.rationale$589: Recording the withdrawal reason supports traceability, diagnostics and continuous improvement, and consistent feedback to other vehicle functions and the driver interface.

fields.name: Re‑Proposal Suppression After Withdrawal
fields.description: After a fastest‑lane‑exit lane‑change proposal is withdrawn, the Dynamic Lane Change function shall suppress generation of a new fastest‑lane‑exit proposal for at least the configured suppression time.
fields.rationale$589: A suppression period prevents rapid on/off cycling of proposals, which could confuse the driver, impair usability, or reduce behavioral stability.

fields.name: Prevent Time‑Based-Only Cancellation of Fastest‑Lane‑Exit Proposal
fields.description: The Dynamic Lane Change function shall prevent cancellation of a fastest‑lane‑exit lane‑change proposal based on elapsed time alone.
fields.rationale$589: Preventing time‑based cancellation ensures that the fastest‑lane‑exit proposal remains active until a clearly defined withdrawal condition occurs. This avoids unintended proposal removal caused solely by passage of time, maintains consistent behavior required for compliance with lane‑usage regulations, and ensures the driver receives stable and predictable guidance.

fields.name: Detect upcoming exit / Service Plaza / Rest Area
fields.description:
The Navigation DOT subsystem shall maintain, as internal state, the type, along-route distance, and estimated time-to-reach for the nearest upcoming exit or Service Plaza / Rest Area on the currently traveled route, computed from map-based long spatial information and ego vehicle state.
 

Inputs:

  • Long Spatial Information from MapService, including exit and Service Plaza / Rest Area data for the current route.
  • Ego vehicle position and motion information (e.g., route position, speed) from upstream subsystems.

Outputs:

  • Internal state values (event type, along-route distance, estimated time-to-reach) available to Navigation DOT timing logic.
fields.rationale$589: The subsystem needs internal knowledge of the nearest upcoming exit or Service Plaza / Rest Area and when it will be reached in order to time Driving Operation Transition requests appropriately.

fields.name: Normal DOT request before exit / Service Plaza / Rest Area
fields.description:
When an exit or Service Plaza / Rest Area exists ahead on the currently traveled route and both the predicted time to reach the associated DOT terminal point is less than or equal to the configurable parameter LP_DOT_NORMAL_LENGTH_SEC (seconds) and the remaining along-route distance to that DOT terminal point is less than or equal to the configurable parameter LP_MARGIN_BEFORE_TERMINAL_METER (meters), the Navigation DOT subsystem shall output DOT request (normal) as true, and it shall output DOT request (normal) as false otherwise.
 

Inputs

  • Internal event state: upcoming exit or Service Plaza / Rest Area, associated DOT terminal point, predicted time-to-reach, remaining distance.
  • Ego vehicle motion information used for the prediction (e.g., speed, acceleration).
  • Calibration parameters:
    • LP_DOT_NORMAL_LENGTH_SEC (time threshold, in seconds).
    • LP_MARGIN_BEFORE_TERMINAL_METER (distance margin, in meters).

Outputs

  • DOT request (normal) signal to ADStateManager.
fields.rationale$589: Issuing a normal DOT request within a defined time and distance window before the DOT terminal point enables a controlled handover from automated driving to the driver before the road section with automated driving availability ends at an exit or Service Plaza / Rest Area.

fields.name: Weak DOT request before exit / Service Plaza / Rest Area
fields.description:
When the predicted time until DOT request (normal) caused by an upcoming exit or Service Plaza / Rest Area on the currently traveled route is greater than or equal to zero and less than or equal to the configurable parameter LP_DOT_WEAK_LENGTH_SEC (seconds), the Navigation DOT subsystem shall output DOT request (weak) as true, and it shall output DOT request (weak) as false otherwise.

Inputs

  • Predicted activation time of DOT request (normal) due to an upcoming exit or Service Plaza / Rest Area.
  • Current time used to compute the prediction horizon.
  • Calibration parameter LP_DOT_WEAK_LENGTH_SEC (prediction window, in seconds).

Outputs

  • DOT request (weak) signal to ADStateManager.
fields.rationale$589: A weak DOT request provides an earlier, lower-intensity indication that a normal DOT request will soon be issued near an exit or Service Plaza / Rest Area, improving driver preparedness for the handover.

fields.name: Silent DOT request before exit / Service Plaza / Rest Area
fields.description:
When the predicted time until DOT request (weak) caused by an upcoming exit or Service Plaza / Rest Area on the currently traveled route is greater than or equal to zero and less than or equal to the configurable parameter LP_DOT_SILENT_LENGTH_SEC (seconds), the Navigation DOT subsystem shall output DOT request (silent) as true, and it shall output DOT request (silent) as false otherwise.

Inputs

  • Predicted activation time of DOT request (weak) due to an upcoming exit or Service Plaza / Rest Area.
  • Current time used to compute the prediction horizon.
  • Calibration parameter LP_DOT_SILENT_LENGTH_SEC (prediction window, in seconds).

Outputs

  • DOT request (silent) signal to ADStateManager.
fields.rationale$589: Silent DOT is the earliest stage in the DOT sequence, enabling downstream functions to prepare for an upcoming driver handover triggered by an exit or Service Plaza / Rest Area before any visible DOT indication is presented.

fields.name: DOT Reason for exit / Service Plaza / Rest Area
fields.description:
When any of DOT request (silent), DOT request (weak), or DOT request (normal) is true and the cause of that DOT request is an upcoming exit or Service Plaza / Rest Area on the currently traveled route, the Navigation DOT subsystem shall output DOT Reason (Exit, Service Plaza / Rest Area) as true, and it shall output DOT Reason (Exit, Service Plaza / Rest Area) as false otherwise.

Inputs

  • DOT request (silent) state and associated cause classification.
  • DOT request (weak) state and associated cause classification.
  • DOT request (normal) state and associated cause classification.

Outputs

  • DOT Reason (Exit, Service Plaza / Rest Area) signal to ADStateManager.
fields.rationale$589: Explicitly indicating that the active DOT request is caused by an upcoming exit or Service Plaza / Rest Area allows downstream logic and HMI to select behaviors and messages that match the DOT cause, and distinguishes this case from other DOT reasons.
